543419|2026-06.headline: Shriram Properties posted record Q1 FY27 sales of INR484 crores (+10% YoY) but revenue of INR271 crores (+4%) and PAT of INR11 crores lag, with growth back-ended.
543419|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 sales value rose 10% YoY to INR484 crores on 0.85 million sq ft, the company's highest-ever Q1, driven by launches at Shriram Stellar (Chennai), Shriram Southbrook (Kolkata) and Green Meadows phase (Chennai). Revenue of INR271 crores, EBITDA of INR42 crores and PAT of INR11 crores were steady, with margins diluted by low-margin legacy Kolkata handovers. Management reiterated full-year FY27 guidance, pointing to Q2 and H2 OCs (about 2,900 units, INR1,560 crores revenue potential) and a back-ended launch calendar. Net debt to equity stood at 0.29x, with gearing expected to rise in FY27.

financial_highlights.metric: Free cash flow before new project investment
Closing cash / gross external debt / net debt
financial_highlights.value: INR219 crores / INR651 crores / INR432 crores

segments.name: Chennai
segments.commentary: Shriram Stellar, a premium launch late June, sold about 20% on launch weekend; Green Meadows new phase (0.2 million sq ft) also launched.

segments.name: Kolkata
segments.commentary: Shriram Southbrook (0.4 million sq ft) launched; branded plotted development had about 55% of inventory sold within 30 days. Legacy Grand One and Sunshine One handovers carry thin margins.

segments.name: Bengaluru / Pune
segments.commentary: Doddagubbi JDA (about 0.7 million sq ft saleable) added in Q1, expected on board end-Q3/early Q4; Manjari (Pune, 2.3 million sq ft via FSI purchase) expected to launch after plan approval.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance unchanged: sales value INR3,300-3,500 crores (40-50% growth) and collections INR2,100-2,200 crores (26-30% growth), per Q&A.
Revenue recognition expected to grow at least 20% in FY27; PAT growth guided at 20-25%; FY27 PBT margin about 8-9%.
FY28 mission reiterated: sales value about INR5,000 crores, revenue INR2,500 crores, PBT about INR250 crores (around 10% margin); FY28 EBITDA margin guided at 22-24%.

Handover pipeline: 410+ units of pent-up handovers, 2 projects (400+ units, INR160 crores) for OC in Q2, and 5+ projects (2,100+ units, INR1,000 crores) for H2; total 2,900+ units, INR1,560 crores revenue potential for balance of FY27.
Management expects gearing to rise temporarily in FY27, with long-term comfort at 0.5x-1.0x net debt to equity.
Management reiterated FY27 sustenance sales of INR1,400-1,500 crores; launch GDV of about INR6,000 crores from 7.23 million sq ft targeted supply.
capex_capacity: FY27 launch calendar: about 6 million sq ft planned out of 7 million sq ft potential across Bengaluru, Chennai, Pune and Kolkata; 2 projects (0.7 million sq ft) launched in Q1.

Current pipeline 33.7 million sq ft (16 million ongoing, 17.7 million upcoming) with GDV potential about INR13,530 crores; 7.3 million sq ft (GDV above INR6,000 crores) at advanced stage for addition in 3-6 months.
Kolkata: about 110 acres of land; 2.3 million sq ft apartment approval obtained pre-election, to be released in phases of 750,000-800,000 sq ft, with only one phase possible in FY27.
Management targets nearly doubling the upcoming pipeline over 18-24 months.
Cash flow: INR88 crores invested in new projects in Q1.
demand_pricing: Sustenance sales prices rising about 4-5% annually, versus 10-15% in the post-COVID period; launch prices set by competition in each micro-market.
Average mid-market selling price about INR7,600-7,700 per sq ft, versus about INR5,000 pre-COVID; Sunshine 2 and 3 realising about INR7,600-7,700 per sq ft.
Management sees no material slowdown in conversion or housing loan application momentum; Bengaluru launches described as slow, upper-end investment demand flagged as softer.
Legacy Shankari (Chennai) and Grand One (Kolkata) realise about INR4,500-5,000 and INR18-24 lakh tickets, dragging margins.

qa_highlights.question: Is the FY28 mission (INR5,000 crores sales, INR2,500 crores revenue, INR250 crores PBT) still intact and how credible is a 10% PBT margin versus historic EBITDA of 7-8%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed the targets. EBITDA margin was 22.5% (FY23), 22.6% (FY24), 18.4% (FY25) and about 13.5% (FY26), with PBT of 8.8%, 7.7%, 9% and about 5.3%. It guided FY28 EBITDA margin of 22-24% and PBT around 10%, based on project-level build-up and not land sales.

qa_highlights.question: Why is sales value growing 40-50% while collections grow only 26-30%?
qa_highlights.answer: Collections follow project progress: 10% on booking, 20% after agreement, then construction-linked. Launches are back-ended to Q3-Q4, so collections ramp in later quarters and FY28.

qa_highlights.question: What is the split of FY27 launch GDV versus sustenance sales?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said sustenance sales of INR1,400-1,500 crores look right; the balance comes from new launches off about 7.23 million sq ft supply worth about INR6,000 crores.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Kolkata land plan and value?
qa_highlights.answer: About 104-106 acres approved for apartments, villas and plots, with a 3-year build and 5-year handover target. Management estimates INR6.5-7.5 crores net contribution per acre and INR1,200-1,400 crores free cash over about five years; bulk sale at INR3.5-4 crores per acre was rejected as uneconomic.

qa_highlights.question: Is the FY27 PBT margin 10% and what drives the margin recovery?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 PBT margin guided at 8-9%. Margins are product-mix driven: Grand One, Shankari and Sunshine One handovers are low-margin, with Sunshine 2 and 3 and post-2019 launches expected to restore mid-20s EBITDA margin and 9-10% PBT, mainly in H2 FY27 and FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Will tax write-backs boost PAT in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said tax write-backs cannot be predicted; they arise only from loss-making subsidiaries recognising deferred tax assets. PAT growth guided at 20-25% without a write-back assumption.

risks_watch: Margin delivery: FY26 EBITDA margin fell to about 13.5% and PBT to about 5.3%; FY27 PBT guided at 8-9% and FY28 PBT ~INR250 crores (~10%) depends on product mix shift to post-2019 launches, which management said may not show until H2 FY27 and FY28.

Revenue timing: Q2 OCs cover 2 projects (400+ units, INR160 crores) and H2 covers 5+ projects (2,100+ units, INR1,000 crores); any slippage in OC timing would push the INR1,560 crores handover potential and the 20%+ revenue growth.

Back-ended sales and collections: FY27 sales INR3,300-3,500 crores and collections INR2,100-2,200 crores rely on Q3-Q4 launches (Manjari pending Pune plan approval, T-John pending plan sanction), so approval delays would hit both.
Balance sheet: gearing expected to rise temporarily in FY27 (net debt to equity 0.29x today, long-term comfort 0.5x-1.0x); debt cost about 11%.

Kolkata monetisation: 2.3 million sq ft apartment approval to be released in phases of 750,000-800,000 sq ft, with only one phase possibly in FY27; land plan economics (INR6.5-7.5 crores per acre net contribution) are management estimates; bulk sale rejected.
Demand: Bengaluru launches slow and upper-end investment demand softer; management sees no material conversion slowdown, but watch launch absorption in Bengaluru and Pune.
key_quotes: Yes, the numbers are right. And Kolkata land sale is not a significant part of it.
We are looking at PBT stabilizing in the range of about 10% margin.
So, this year, we might be in the 8% to 9%.

Tax write-back is difficult to predict because tax write-back happen only when there is a project where we are having a loss that is being recognized, there's a deferred asset getting created only then the tax write-back happens in the joint venture
543419|2026-06.management_tone: Management is confident on the full-year FY27 guidance and the FY28 mission, backed by handover visibility and the launch calendar, but cautious on timing: revenue and margin recovery is repeatedly placed in H2 and FY28. It was defensive on EBITDA-to-PBT comparability and on the 10% PBT target, and evasive on tax write-backs and on Kolkata land monetisation timing.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: EBITDA margin fell to about 13.5% in FY26 from 18.4% in FY25; management guides FY27 PBT margin at 8-9% and FY28 EBITDA margin at 22-24%, driven by mix shift to Sunshine 2/3 and post-2019 launches at about 7,600-7,700/sq ft versus low-margin legacy handovers.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Doddagubbi JDA (about 0.7 million sq ft) expected on board end-Q3/early Q4 and Manjari (2.3 million sq ft) to launch in Q3 after plan approval; about 6 million sq ft of 7 million sq ft launch potential planned for FY27, with 7.3 million sq ft at advanced stage for addition in 3-6 months.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Q1 sales volume was 0.85 million sq ft (+4% YoY) with sales value up 10%, and 2,900+ units of handovers in Q2 (400+ units) and H2 (2,100+ units) drive revenue recognition growth of at least 20% in FY27.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management targets nearly doubling the upcoming pipeline over 18-24 months from 17.7 million sq ft, and 7.3 million sq ft (GDV above INR6,000 crores) is at advanced stage, but Kolkata phases of 750,000-800,000 sq ft allow only one phase in FY27 and utilisation is not a disclosed metric.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 sales guidance of INR3,300-3,500 crores was held rather than raised, and management said FY27 PAT growth excludes any tax write-back, with launches back-ended to Q3-Q4.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: H2 covers 5+ projects (2,100+ units, INR1,000 crores) of the INR1,560 crores handover potential, and Manjari and T-John depend on pending plan approvals; a slip would hit revenue growth of at least 20% and the Q3-Q4 launch-led sales and collections.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Launches in Q1 (Shriram Stellar, Shriram Southbrook 0.4 million sq ft, Green Meadows phase 0.2 million sq ft) with about 6 million sq ft of FY27 launches planned and Manjari (2.3 million sq ft) after approval; Bengaluru launches described as slow.

rows.label: Sales value FY27 INR3,300-3,500 crores (40-50% growth)
rows.why: Q1 sales of INR484 crores (+10% YoY) is back-ended, so FY27 needs roughly INR2,800-3,000 crores more over Q2-Q4 from launches of about 6 million sq ft and sustenance sales of INR1,400-1,500 crores.

rows.label: Gearing rises temporarily in FY27
rows.why: Net debt to equity at 0.29x (net debt INR432 crores on equity INR1,471 crores) with management expecting temporary rise toward long-term comfort of 0.5x-1.0x, and debt cost about 11%.

rows.label: Sustenance price growth 4-5% annually
rows.why: Sustenance prices rising about 4-5% per year versus 10-15% post-COVID, and average mid-market price about INR7,600-7,700 per sq ft versus about INR5,000 pre-COVID.

tone.note: Management was confident on FY27 guidance held at INR3,300-3,500 crores sales and the FY28 mission (INR5,000 crores sales, INR250 crores PBT), but cautious on timing with recovery placed in H2 and FY28; analysts pushed on the 10% PBT margin versus FY26 PBT of about 5.3%, while management was evasive

543420|2026-09.headline: Jet Freight H1 FY27 revenue about ₹297 Cr, with PAT margin near 1.5% and management guiding FY27 revenue to ₹580–600 Cr.
543420|2026-09.overview: Management presented H1 FY27 (six months to 30 September 2026) revenue of about ₹297 Cr, with EBITDA margin of about 4.58% and PAT margin of about 1.52% (CFO also cited 1.55%). Shipments rose from 430 to 674 and tonnage from 545 to 744 tons year on year, with tonnage up about 32.84%. Management said it expects to close FY27 at ₹580–600 Cr revenue and targets roughly double the PAT margin, with H1 EBITDA cited as ₹12.5 Cr. Strategic items discussed were a proposed Dubai acquisition (NatWest), retail courier launch, ocean freight build-out, South America entry and a planned booking platform.

segments.name: Perishables (agro, fresh, temperature-controlled)
segments.commentary: About 45% of revenue; management calls it a niche, time-sensitive business where the company is the largest in India by volume, including mangoes to US and UK and roses.

segments.name: General cargo (incl. courier and e-commerce)
segments.commentary: Courier and e-commerce estimated at 25–30% of general cargo volumes; 98% of business is international per management.

segments.name: Ocean freight
segments.commentary: Small today (sea imports described as negligible); centralised in a Delhi team and targeted for growth in bulk and rice, with no revenue target given.

segments.name: Air import and sea import
segments.commentary: Described as negligible; management plans to build these over time.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue expected at ₹580–600 Cr.
Management aims to roughly double PAT margin from current levels; H1 EBITDA cited at ₹12.5 Cr.
Retail courier (B2C) launched in October 2026 after wholesale courier business; no revenue target given.
Tech platform (booking and rate engine for franchisees) expected to be ready by end-2026, per management.
Dubai acquisition (NatWest) not yet completed; management sees little contribution in FY27 and significant growth in FY28.
Management expects fuel-driven freight rate pressure to persist at least until end-2026.
capex_capacity: All warehouses are leased; the company owns no land or warehouses and operates an asset-light model with surface transport outsourced.
Current infrastructure can handle about double the present business volume, per management, so costs should stay flat as volumes rise.
Ocean freight team centralised in a large Delhi office; 8–9 major shipping lines are key carrier partners.
South America: a senior hire made in Brazil, with a back-office team in India; local operations are to follow in about a year if volumes build.
Dubai acquisition (NatWest) under way to take charter brokering and Gulf/Saudi business in-house.
demand_pricing: Management says it passes through freight cost changes and maintains margins; industry margins quoted at 10–25%, sometimes 7–8%.
Freight rate increases are route-specific (e.g., routing constraints and war-related), and fuel prices drive freight costs.
Growth partly from new e-commerce shops and end consumers, plus organic growth from existing customers; one customer's volume reportedly doubled.
Charter demand from Gulf supermarkets (e.g., Lulu, Nesto) rose, with about 70 charters since March, per management.

qa_highlights.question: How does the e-commerce and courier business operate, its domestic/international mix, revenue and EBITDA contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 98% of business is international, mainly wholesale consolidation to US, UK, Europe, Australia and NZ; retail B2B/B2C is starting. No revenue or EBITDA split was given.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 96% air, perishable and general cargo mix intended to be maintained, or will ocean, courier and others grow?
qa_highlights.answer: Courier sits within general cargo. Management said ocean freight must be pursued for sheer scale, but it will be taken slowly.

qa_highlights.question: Dubai acquisition: business mix, geographic coverage, synergies, valuation, and financial impact?
qa_highlights.answer: The target (NatWest) covers UAE, Gulf and Saudi. Valuation was based on future orders from its promoters' linked customers. The deal is not complete, so no FY27 impact is expected.

qa_highlights.question: Ocean freight: capabilities, carrier partnerships and medium-term revenue target?
qa_highlights.answer: Ocean team is centralised in Delhi; relationships with about 8–9 major shipping lines. No medium-term revenue target was given.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the 41% Q2 YoY revenue growth came from volume versus price?
qa_highlights.answer: No split was given. Management cited a sales process for volume growth and route-specific pricing, with fuel costs affecting freight rates.

qa_highlights.question: Courier shipments and tonnage decreased YoY; what is the driver?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed growth to new routes (direct flights to destinations like Germany), new e-commerce customers and organic growth at existing customers.

qa_highlights.question: Brazil/South America: current stage and milestones?
qa_highlights.answer: A senior person hired in Brazil; inquiries have turned into some business. Own operations are possible in about a year once volumes increase.

qa_highlights.question: Does the company own land, and will margins improve with volume?
qa_highlights.answer: No land is owned and all warehouses are leased. Management expects margins and bottom line to rise quarter on quarter as costs stay flat.

risks_watch: Revenue split between volume and price for the 41% Q2 YoY growth was not disclosed.
Dubai acquisition (NatWest) valuation rests on future orders and is incomplete; NatWest revenue reportedly below ₹1 Cr.
Fuel-linked freight rate volatility and geopolitical route disruption could affect margins.
Thin PAT margin of about 1.5% leaves little buffer against cost swings.
Courier volume decline YoY was raised by an analyst but only partly reconciled by management.
Retail courier and tech platform (end-2026) are unproven; ocean freight and South America remain early-stage.
543420|2026-09.management_tone: Confident and expansive on growth plans and margin outlook, but answers were often unstructured and gave few quantified targets (no ocean revenue target, no acquisition financials, no volume/price split).
key_quotes: Whatever our margins are, even if the Freight is double, tripled, we'll still maintain our margins.
Currently, we do not have any warehouses that are owned, everything is leased.
So, margin, bottom line, you will see increasing quarter on quarter and year on year, definitely.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management says it aims to roughly double the PAT margin from about 1.5% and expects margins to rise quarter on quarter as costs stay flat, but fuel-driven freight rate pressure is expected to persist at least until end-2026 and the H1 EBITDA margin is only 4.58%.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: All warehouses are leased, no land or owned warehouses, and existing infrastructure is said to handle about double current volume, so no new physical capacity is quantified in the window.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: H1 FY27 tonnage rose about 32.84% (545 to 744 tons) and shipments about 56% (430 to 674), with ~70 Gulf charters since March and one customer's volume reportedly doubling, supporting the ₹580-600 Cr FY27 revenue guide.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Asset-light model with all warehouses leased and no capex discussed; infrastructure said to handle about double current volume, so utilisation pressure is not evident.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 revenue guided to ₹580-600 Cr with H1 EBITDA at ₹12.5 Cr, but the brief gives no implied H2 run-rate and the 41% Q2 YoY growth was not split between volume and price.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Thin 1.5% PAT margin leaves little buffer, and fuel-linked freight rate pressure is expected to persist at least until end-2026; the courier volume decline YoY was only partly reconciled.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Retail B2C courier launched in October 2026 and a tech booking/rate platform is expected by end-2026, but neither has a revenue target and both are unproven.

rows.label: Dubai acquisition (NatWest) and South America entry
rows.why: Dubai deal is not complete with little FY27 contribution expected and NatWest revenue reportedly below ₹1 Cr; South America has a senior hire in Brazil with local operations possible in about a year if volumes build.

rows.label: Ocean freight build-out
rows.why: Ocean freight is small today, centralised in Delhi with 8-9 shipping lines, and targeted for bulk and rice growth, but no revenue target was given and it will be taken slowly.

rows.label: Fuel-driven route-specific freight rate pressure
rows.why: Management expects fuel-driven freight rate pressure to persist at least until end-2026, and says it passes through cost changes while industry margins run 7-25%.

tone.note: Management was confident on FY27 revenue of ₹580-600 Cr, margin doubling and new ventures, but was vague on the volume/price split, Dubai financials and ocean targets, while analysts pressed on the courier volume decline and the mix of the 41% Q2 growth.

543425|2026-03.headline: MapmyIndia Q4 FY26: revenue up 54.8% QoQ, EBITDA margin 44.6% (+460 bps YoY), but FY26 revenue only INR474 crore vs INR463 crore.
543425|2026-03.overview: Management reported a sharp sequential Q4 recovery: revenue up 54.8% QoQ, EBITDA up 141% QoQ, PAT up 171% QoQ, with EBITDA margin at 44.6% and PAT margin at 31.3%. Full-year FY26 growth was muted, with revenue moving from INR463 crore to INR474 crore, as government contracts were delayed or deferred into FY27. Management attributed the Q4 shortfall against its own expectations (about INR45-50 crore by an analyst's estimate) to customer-side delays of roughly INR20 crore in an automotive IoT order plus government push-outs, all described as timing rather than lost business. Management reiterated the INR1,000 crore FY28 roadmap and an order book of about INR1,750 crore, but gave no formal FY27 growth guidance.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR463 crore in FY25 (c.1-2% growth)

financial_highlights.value: INR3.50 per share (175% on INR2 face value)

financial_highlights.change: vs INR133 crore in March 2025 (per analyst)

segments.name: A&M (Automotive & Mobility)
segments.commentary: Grew about 9% for FY26 per management. Q4 automotive core business described as soft by an analyst; management said a Hyundai-related variation was a drag, while attach rates and program presence rose YoY.

segments.name: C&E (Consumer & Enterprise, incl. Government)
segments.commentary: Declined about 3% for FY26, which management attributed to government contracts delayed into FY27. C&E rose 142% QoQ in Q4. Government open order book closed above INR200 crore; government billing crossed INR100 crore and cash collection crossed INR100 crore in FY26.

segments.name: IoT-led business
segments.commentary: Management said IoT EBITDA margin rose from 14% in FY25 to 16% in FY26, with Q4 margin at about 33%. Management called this a quarterly high driven by operating leverage and a better SaaS mix, not a one-off.

segments.name: Mappls App
segments.commentary: Cumulative downloads above 45 million, with 10+ million added during FY26. Amazon Now was cited as a corporate API/SDK integration example, with rollout in Bengaluru and Mumbai.

guidance_outlook: Management is confident of growth 'above 20%' in FY27 per the 5-year trajectory, and an analyst asked whether 25% growth is achievable; management said there was 'no reason not to believe' 25% growth is possible but gave no formal number.
INR1,000 crore revenue roadmap for FY28 is unchanged; timing is under review year by year.
Open order book about INR1,750 crore (including 18% GST); billing about INR520 crore and sales about INR470 crore in the order book breakup.
Management expects the INR20 crore IoT order delayed in Q4 to reflect in Q1 and Q2 FY27, and government push-outs to Q1-Q2 FY27.
Management plans to change segment reporting from FY27 Q1 to Auto & Retail, Corporate and Government, with restated FY26 quarterly figures.
Management targets IoT EBITDA margin above 16% in FY27 and sees steady-state IoT margins above 16%.
capex_capacity: Capital allocation in FY26 was about INR120 crore for organic growth (government, IoT, intellectual property); small acquisitions were minor.
IoT hardware is capitalised as fixed assets and depreciated over 3 years under the opex subscription model, so IoT growth needs capital.

Inventory of IoT devices rose to support expected demand; management said purchases are based on portfolio forecasts, not specific orders, and that hardware price inflation is being offset through pricing and value engineering.
Government business requires working capital, mainly receivables, to fund delayed payments at Mappls DT and Gtropy.
No specific capex amount for FY27 was given.
demand_pricing: FY26 open order book began at about INR1,500 crore; about 18% (c.INR270 crore) converted to revenue, and INR780 crore of in-year new orders produced about INR200 crore of in-year revenue (about 25%).
Management said the FY26 conversion rate could be 'higher' in FY27, but gave no number.

Fixed-price contracts are used in government (milestone-based), corporate (lump-sum or minimum guarantee) and IoT (fixed fleet size or minimum guarantee, 3-5 year SaaS terms). Management described fixed-price visibility as 'very clear', with volume contracts historically flexing up.

Government receivables: management said there have been almost no bad debts in government, but collection periods are longer. Trade receivables rose from INR133 crore to INR176 crore YoY (per analyst), against flat revenue.
Management said a government 'Large Energy response system' order and a large government IoT tender (re-tendered) were delayed, outside its control.

qa_highlights.question: Why was there a weak full-year performance in automotive/mobility and consumer-enterprise, and what is the FY27 outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said total FY26 revenue was INR474 crore vs INR463 crore; C&E fell about 3% because government work was delayed and A&M grew about 9%. Q4 C&E rose 142% QoQ. The government order book is above INR200 crore, and management is confident of significant growth in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the order book to revenue conversion outlook for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 conversion was about 18% of the INR1,500 crore opening book. Management declined to give a fixed range but said FY27 could be higher.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capital allocation plan for the roughly INR600 crore cash?
qa_highlights.answer: Organic growth comes first (IoT, government, IP). IoT hardware is capitalised and depreciated over 3 years, and government needs working capital. No acquisition, dividend or buyback plan was detailed beyond the FY26 final dividend.

qa_highlights.question: Where was the Q4 revenue shortfall of about INR45-50 crore vs expectations?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a roughly INR20 crore automotive IoT order delayed by customer regulatory requirements (now fulfilled, expected in Q1-Q2), a government Large Energy Response order delayed by the government, and a large government IoT tender sent to re-tender. Management called these push-outs, not lost business.

qa_highlights.question: Why is core C&E flat, and will the segment reporting change?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the corporate API/SDK revenue ramps with usage (Amazon Now cited), with a gestation period. Segment reporting will move to Auto & Retail, Corporate and Government from Q1 FY27 with restated quarterly FY26 figures.

qa_highlights.question: Why did trade receivables rise and is there a collection concern?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said government receivables reflect a longer collection cycle with no material bad debt; Mappls DT collected prior-year receivables, with overdue amounts expected to be lower than total receivables. DSO was described as better than industry.

qa_highlights.question: Why did IoT margins rise to about 33% in Q4 and is inventory a factor?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the margin to operating leverage, better mix (more SaaS) and cost optimisation, and denied inventory gains. Inventory rose to meet expected IoT demand. Management targets IoT EBITDA margin above 16% in FY27.

risks_watch: Execution timing: revenue conversion is lumpy and dependent on customer readiness and government approvals; Q4 slippage of about INR45-50 crore by analyst estimate.
Receivables: trade receivables rose about 32% YoY to INR176 crore against flat revenue; watch DSO and government collections in Q1 FY27.
IoT input cost inflation (DRAM/NAND prices cited by an analyst) versus rising IoT margins; watch whether margins hold and whether inventory-linked gains recur.
Geopolitical and government budget pressure cited by an analyst; management said it saw no change to business as usual.
Revenue CAGR of 1-2% in FY26 versus the 25-30% growth an analyst asked about; watch Q1 FY27 for conversion to a FY27 growth rate and the FY28 INR1,000 crore target.
Segment reporting change from Q1 FY27 will affect comparability.
543425|2026-03.management_tone: Management was confident and upbeat about the Q4 inflection and FY27 pipeline, but became defensive and less specific when pressed on the FY26 shortfall, the revenue gap, and receivables. It gave no quantified FY27 guidance and declined to name accounts or quantify the delayed government orders.
key_quotes: Q4 marked a positive inflection point with improving business activity and stronger execution.
So our road map continues with INR1,000 crores. The team, the entire leadership team is working on it.
The gap is maybe 5 accounts or 6 accounts, but the orders exist.
Our first priority, which we believe is the right way to do is to provide organic growth.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin 44.6% (+460 bps YoY) and IoT margin about 33% in Q4 vs 16% FY26; management targets IoT EBITDA margin above 16% in FY27, though Q4 level is a quarterly high and IoT input costs (DRAM/NAND) are rising.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: No new plant, line or branch capacity was discussed; IoT device inventory was built for expected demand but no capacity addition was guided.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Open order book about INR1,750 crore with government order book above INR200 crore; FY26 conversion was about 18% of the INR1,500 crore opening book, and management says FY27 conversion could be higher, with growth above 20% expected and 25% possible.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: FY26 capital allocation was about INR120 crore for organic growth and IoT hardware is capitalised, but no FY27 capex amount was given and utilisation was not disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Why not guide to 20% growth when demand is improving?

qa_highlights.question: What drove the PAT margin decline and when does PAT growth return to mid-to-high teens?

qa_highlights.question: Is BIS relief helping FILA launch timelines, and how is FILA inventory being discounted?

543426|2026-09.headline: Metro Brands Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 12.2% to INR730 crore, with EBITDA up 15.9% to INR198 crore, while festive demand shifted into Q3.
543426|2026-09.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 12.2% to INR730 crore and EBITDA rose 15.9% to INR198 crore, with margin at 27.1% versus 26.2% a year ago. PAT grew about 11% to INR77 crore with margin flat at 10.6%, as higher rentals, staff costs and marketing, plus lower treasury income, offset a gross margin gain. Management attributed much of the revenue slowdown to festive demand moving from September into October, and said net store additions were slowed to 12 in Q2 with selective openings. Newer brands (Clarks, Foot Locker, MetroActiv, FILA) remain constrained by BIS-related supply issues and are being scaled cautiously.

segments.name: Crocs
segments.commentary: Crocs is under 20% of total business across stores, Metro and Mochi multi-brand. Management said Crocs grew decently and Durga Puja/Shraddh timing, not Crocs, drove the quarter.

segments.name: Clarks
segments.commentary: Women's range in more than 400 multi-brand outlets and limited men's range in more than 100; full exclusive store range expected in Q3 FY27, exclusive EBO launch targeted in H2 FY27. Clarks had about 80 EBOs in India at one point.

segments.name: FILA
segments.commentary: Local footwear manufacturing started in India in response to BIS concerns; repositioning expected over 12-18 months, with store expansion picking up from FY28.

segments.name: Foot Locker / MetroActiv
segments.commentary: BIS implementation challenges for selected external brands constrained supply and store expansion; early signs of normalisation, with openings calibrated to product availability.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the gross margin gain is sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Lower end-of-season discounts and online sales discounts were the main drivers, with some markup improvement and lower e-commerce mix. Management said discount benefits will not sustain in Q3; mix shift towards Walkway, Foot Locker and MetroActiv may pull gross margin lower over time.

543427|2026-03.headline: MedPlus Q4 FY26: consolidated revenue INR18,644 mn and operating EBITDA margin 5.8%; FY27 plan of 800 net new stores, including franchisees.

543427|2026-06.headline: MedPlus Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue INR18,796 million (pharmacy +21.8% YoY) but operating EBITDA margin fell to 3.5%, and the board-approved capex was put on hold.

Management put the board-approved capex (food park/oil extraction unit and a wellness services facility, about INR40 crore for the food park) on hold after investor pushback, and said the annual operating plan was not changed for now. Net store additions were 146 (131 franchisee), against the 800 net-addition FY27 target.

Management retained its FY27 revenue goal and a 25% EBITDA margin aspiration, while declaring a Rs.168 Crores buyback at Rs.340 per share and completing two acquisitions (Securens closed, FSS signed and expected to close end-Q1 FY27). Management walked away from a Rs.700 Crores transaction-fee ATM contract, citing return thresholds.

qa_highlights.question: Why would banks add offsite ATMs, and how do onsite and offsite economics differ?
qa_highlights.answer: Banks now treat ATMs as an alternate servicing channel; recyclers handle cash acceptance, video KYC and card issuance and replace branch transactions. Banks are increasingly funding capex themselves, which changes the economics for deployers.

qa_highlights.answer: SBI runs 7-10 years, ICICI longer, HDFC about five years. Management suggested dividing total contract value evenly across years for simplicity, noting ramp, price changes and churn will vary.

qa_highlights.answer: Management converted unsecured receivables to secured loans for one MSP, took an escrow route on another and solved a third. Provision already taken in Q2 FY26. Management said there is no further risk expected.

ROCE was about 25% in prior years. Rajiv Kaul said he will not participate in the buyback.

543458|2026-06.headline: Consolidated revenue rose 18% YoY to INR 20,048 crore and operating EBITDA 34% to INR 693 crore in Q1 FY27, with Edible Oil volume only 2%.

Operating EBITDA rose 34% to INR 693 crore, with PBT up 48% and PAT up 40%, which management attributed to a Food-led mix, disciplined pricing and efficiencies. Edible Oil volume grew only 2% due to channel destocking and supply chain issues amid palm oil volatility, while Industry Essentials grew volume 13%. Management said July trends had improved and reiterated FY27 segment operating guidance, and changed segment disclosure to revenue, volume growth and margin for Food and FMCG.

segments.commentary: Volume up 2% YoY due to channel destocking, supply chain disruption and sluggish trade; revenue up 15% and EBITDA per ton up 33% YoY.

segments.name: Industry Essentials

qa_highlights.answer: Management guided double-digit volume and revenue growth, with revenue growth of about 18%-20%; the 6% Q1 margin should not be the benchmark, and the average of the last four to five quarters is the right yardstick given the investment phase.

qa_highlights.question: Dhiraj Mistry: What revenue, margin and royalty terms apply to Madhur, and what are the targets?
qa_highlights.answer: Madhur sells about 15,000 tons/month, targeted at 20,000 tons/month by year end; FY27 revenue estimated at INR 700-800 crore; royalty 0.5% of sales to Shree Renuka Sugars; margin guidance to be in line with the overall Food segment.

qa_highlights.question: Dhiraj Mistry: What Edible Oil volume growth is expected over the medium term and full year?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 volume was hit by destocking, supply chain issues and sluggish trade; management is not guiding 2% and expects 5%-6% volume growth over the remaining nine months, with festive and post-monsoon demand from Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Ashutosh Joytiraditya (ICICI Securities): What capex and market share gains are budgeted for the 2030 vision?
qa_highlights.answer: No specific four-year capex figure; capex will follow capacity needs, with Edible Oil refining at 60%-61% utilisation likely exhausted in a couple of years. Steady-state modelling assumption is about INR 700 crore per year.

qa_highlights.question: Ashutosh Joytiraditya: What efficiencies will the higher Wilmar ownership bring, and how much can domestic oilseed sourcing reduce imports?
qa_highlights.answer: Sourcing efficiency is unchanged; the main new lever is Wilmar's R&D and technical expertise. Management declined to give an import-reduction number, noting about 70% of edible oil requirement is imported and mustard is the focus.

qa_highlights.question: Lakshmi Narayan (Tunga Investments): What share of raw material is imported and from Wilmar, and what is the volume growth outlook? Also, B2C/B2B mix of Food?

qa_highlights.question: Lakshmi Narayan: How are Wilmar transactions priced and what are the stock days and oil mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Wilmar transactions are at arm's length, including pricing and credit period. Raw material stock is 30-35 days; oil mix is about 30% palm, 30%-35% soya, 20% sunflower and 15% local oils.

543458|2026-09.headline: AWL Agri Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 26% YoY to INR22,202 crore on 14% volume growth; normalized EBITDA up 11% to INR623 crore.
543458|2026-09.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 26% YoY to INR22,202 crore on 14% underlying volume growth, and normalized operating EBITDA rose 11% to INR623 crore. PBT grew 4% to INR344 crore while PAT fell 2% to INR239 crore, which management attributed to minimum corporate tax on the Bangladesh subsidiary's revenue. H1 FY27 revenue rose 22% to INR42,250 crore with normalized EBITDA up 25% to INR1,378 crore. Operating cash flow was negative in H1 because about INR6,000 crore of inventory build (sluggish September and sunflower supply disruption) was funded through working capital lines and booked under financing; management expects reversal from Q3.

segments.name: Edible oils
segments.commentary: Volume grew 5% in the quarter with market share maintained, driven by domestic mustard, groundnut and cottonseed oils. EBITDA was about INR4,100 per MT, within the INR4,000-4,500 per MT guidance.

segments.name: Industry Essentials
segments.commentary: Volume grew 25% and EBITDA was INR4,300 per MT, above the INR3,000-3,500 guidance. Oleochemicals and specialty chemicals are about 45% of segment revenue. Management called the 26% growth a one-off tied to de-oiled cake parity, guiding high single to low double-digit growth going forward.

segments.name: Branded exports and Tops
segments.commentary: Branded export grew 72% YoY with LTM revenue near INR800 crore, targeting diaspora markets (US, UK, Europe, Australia). GD Foods (Tops) grew above 25%, with East and Central India expansion planned over the next 1-1.5 years.

Non-funded trade credit (letters of credit for imports) of about INR8,500 crore; management said it should be excluded from net debt.
Direct retail reach 9.7 lakh outlets; total retail reach around 26 lakh outlets; focus shifting to throughput and outlet productivity.

Rainfall deficit of 12-13% nationally, with more than 30% deficits in parts of Rajasthan, Haryana and Punjab; management flagged risk to Kharif harvest and Rabi sowing.
Headline CPI near 6% and food inflation at 7-7.5%, which management said could cause some rural sluggishness, offset by festive demand.
Quick commerce grew 40% YoY; food and FMCG channel mix about 75% general trade and 25% alternate channel, with alternate channels growing faster.
Government cut edible oil import duty in late September; management said brand strength should allow pass-through of inventory cost.
Standardized pack sizes from September seen as favourable for branded players and likely to boost volumes.

qa_highlights.question: Why did operating cash flow turn negative in H1 and when will inventory normalize?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory rose about INR6,000 crore (not INR600 crore) on weak September demand and sunflower supply disruption; funded by working capital lines classified under financing. Expected to correct in the October-November-December quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What EBITDA margin for edible oil and the full year?
qa_highlights.answer: Company-level EBITDA margin was 2.6% currently; management expects close to 3% for the full year, about INR2,600 crore on INR85,000 crore revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 26% Industry Essentials growth sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management called it a one-off tied to de-oiled cake parity; coming quarters should see 10-11% growth.

qa_highlights.question: Can H2 high single-digit volume growth hold despite weak rural demand?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to H1 volume growth of 11% and festive pent-up demand for daily-essential food; full year volume growth expected at 8-9%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did PBT grow only 6% (or 4% per the release) against 14% volume growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed this to mark-to-market timing differences on derivatives between quarters, saying H1 looks better than Q2 and results normalize over longer periods.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of the edible oil import duty cut on inventory-driven profitability?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there should be no material impact because brand strength allows price recovery; some impact is possible but expected to be recovered through pricing.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Industry Essentials demerger planned, and is a buyback possible?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no demerger plan, as oleochemicals are forward integration of palm refining. A buyback was suggested by an analyst; no response was recorded in the transcript.

543463|2026-03.headline: Vedant Fashions Q4 FY26 revenue rose 8.7% to ~INR 399 crore with 65% gross margin, while retail sales grew 7.8% to INR 561 crore and SSG was 4.6%.
543463|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 retail sales (customer sales) reached about INR 561 crore, up 7.8% YoY, with SSG of about 4.6%, and management said most of the quarter's growth came in March. Reported revenue from operations was about INR 399 crore (+8.7%) and PAT about INR 114 crore (+13%). For FY26, retail sales crossed INR 2,000 crore at INR 2,008 crore (+6.1%), but revenue from operations grew only about 3.5% to INR 1,436 crore and PAT was about INR 376 crore. Management guided to mostly SSG-led growth in FY27, with gross openings stable but net store additions still positive, and said the retail-to-net-sales gap is mainly a GST effect that should normalise from FY27.

financial_highlights.change: contraction of ~150 bps per analyst question, not disputed

financial_highlights.metric: Cash conversion FY26 (operating cash flow to PAT, excl. finance income)

segments.commentary: Retail network of about 669 EBO stores across 252 cities and towns, totalling about 1.79 million sq ft as of March 2026. FY26 net area addition was about 4,200 sq ft after closures; gross addition was about 1 lakh sq ft. Twamev has about 8 EBOs and Mohey a similar number; Diwas has no physical stores yet.

Retail-to-net-sales gap (~29% for FY26, primary 71% vs secondary 73% cited) is mainly GST-driven and expected to normalise from FY27, though management said the gap is 'here to stay' at a decent level while growth rates will track.

Input cost: fabric is INR 8-10 of a INR 100 MRP product; expected 50-150 bps increase in total cost, i.e. INR 1-1.5 per INR 100 product. Management said most current SKU orders are placed at existing prices, so gross margin impact should be limited (10-15 bps at most).
Capital allocation: historically ~50% of profit paid as dividend post-IPO; a concrete policy on cash deployment is expected by the next earnings call.
Inorganic: cash is available for acquisitions, but no pipeline; management said the sector's players are too small.
capex_capacity: Gross retail area addition FY26 about 1 lakh sq ft; net addition about 4,200 sq ft after rationalising underperforming stores.
Revenue per sq ft of new stores opened vs stores closed is about 85% higher (management's average comparison for FY26).
About 5-5.5% of retail area is in underperforming stores management wants to exit.
Twamev: sites are mostly build-to-suit with 18-20 month lead time; 5-6 further stores being signed; openings staggered, with some possibly in H1 FY28 or FY29.
Manyavar kurta-only 1,000 sq ft format being piloted in high-throughput Bangalore neighbourhoods; no physical Diwas stores planned in FY27 beyond a possible pilot.
Rentals in new markets (e.g., Bhopal) are 1.3-1.4x management's target levels, which is slowing new openings.
demand_pricing: Footfall improved by low single digits in Q4 and conversion stayed stable at high levels; average basket size rose about 1.5%.
ASP growth lagged over the past 2-3 years; management plans to lift ASP by about 3-3.5% per category through merchandise upgrades, not price hikes.
Management said March was the strongest month and April has been decent; May is affected by Adhik Maas, with July wedding dates expected to help versus FY26.
Consumer sentiment turned neutral after the war began around late Feb/early March 2026.
Competitive intensity: 2022 entrants are closing, while players that entered in the last 1-2 years are still adding stores; net industry store additions are described as nil.
Gross margin contraction for FY26 attributed by management mainly to GST rate changes from September 2025 (blended GST around 10% pre-change, now slightly higher).

qa_highlights.question: How will SSG and new store openings look in FY27, and how will input inflation affect gross margin?
qa_highlights.answer: No SSG guidance; focus on footfall, conversion, ASP and training. Fabric is about INR 8-10 of a INR 100 product, implying 50-150 bps cost pressure, largely offset by existing orders placed at old prices.

qa_highlights.question: Why has the retail-to-net sales gap widened to ~29% in FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Mainly GST after the September 2025 rate revision, which management expects to normalise from FY27. The growth gap between primary and secondary sales was 2-3%.

qa_highlights.question: What share of stores and area is weak, and how much better are new stores?
qa_highlights.answer: About 5-5.5% of retail area is in weak stores versus a normal closure rate of 2-3%. New stores' revenue per sq ft is about 85% higher than closed stores (FY26 averages).

qa_highlights.question: Will there be a capital return or inorganic move?
qa_highlights.answer: Historically about 50% of profit paid as dividend; a concrete policy is expected by the next call. No acquisition pipeline, though cash is available.

qa_highlights.question: Is Twamev going to scale from 8 stores to 30 in the coming year?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Build-to-suit leases mean an 18-20 month lag; openings are staggered and some may come in H1 FY28 or FY29. Management declined to commit to 30 stores.

543463|2026-06.headline: Vedant Fashions Q1 FY27 revenue from operations rose 7.2% to INR3,014 mn, with PAT up 14.7% to about INR81 crore and domestic SSG at 3.8%.
543463|2026-06.overview: Management reported Q1 FY27 retail sales (customer sales) of INR4,195 mn, up 3.4% YoY, with domestic SSG ex-SIS of about 3.8%. Revenue from operations was about INR3,014 mn (INR301 crore), up 7.2%, with gross margin of 65.7% and EBITDA margin of 44.6%. EBITDA grew 10.8% and PAT margin was 26.7%. Store closures were elevated in Q1 by design, with openings pushed to H2, and management said closures and competitor exits are reducing industry store count in about 8 top states.

financial_highlights.change: vs 65.0% in Q4 FY26; YoY decline attributed partly to GST

financial_highlights.metric: Cash conversion (TTM June 2026, OCF/PAT excl. finance income)

segments.name: Manyavar / Mohey (core and non-bridal push)
segments.commentary: Mohey is growing faster than company average; push into stitched suits, sarees and crop-top lehengas. Manyavar's mega campaign with Rashmika Mandanna and Vijay Deverakonda reportedly exceeded 1 billion views.

segments.name: Twamev (premium)
segments.commentary: Management said Twamev outperformed the company in overall growth in Q1.

segments.name: Diwas
segments.commentary: Launched about a year ago; Q1 not reflective of its progress. Majority of MBO/SIS bookings for Q2 done; e-commerce deals signed with Myntra, Amazon, Blinkit and Zepto.

segments.name: MBO + SIS + e-commerce
segments.commentary: Together about 5% of revenue today; new leadership team built and growth targets described as aggressive. SIS is a few hundred sq ft versus EBO average of about 3,000 sq ft.

segments.name: International (UAE, North America)
segments.commentary: Under pressure: UAE affected by war, North America by tariffs. No growth figures given.

guidance_outlook: Core goal is a strong SSG in FY27; management said a net positive store count for the year is expected despite closures.
Gross openings to be concentrated in H2 (end of Q2 and early Q3), with openings at about 3-4% of store base as a typical annual tail; openings to accelerate as rental pressure eases.
Revenue growth target for FY27 relies on SSG, productivity uplift from new versus closed stores, net openings and MBO/SIS/e-commerce growth.
Asked about high-single-digit SSG for the remaining nine months: management called it a fair understanding and said FY27 will still be net positive.
ASP growth ambition slightly above plan; expected to start materialising from mid-Q2. Q1 SSG was split roughly half volume and half price.
Wedding calendar: November to March expected to be fantastic; October may be weaker YoY because Navratri was pushed by Adhik maas; January has wedding dates this year versus none last year.
capex_capacity: Q1 closures were deliberately front-loaded; management avoids carrying loss-making stores into the Q2 off-season, with openings aimed at H2.

Franchisee capex: about INR2,100-2,150 per sq ft in Tier 2/3 cities and about INR2,500 per sq ft in Tier 1.
Franchisee revenue break-even benchmarks per sq ft: about INR7,000 (Tier 3), INR8,500 (Tier 2), INR10,000-10,500 (Tier 1). Management said franchisee ROI is currently good.

Celebration wear dead stock is hard to liquidate at a discount, so management expects weaker players to exit, mainly regional and local ones.
Management said it is too early to link competitor closures to its own growth and wants 2-3 more quarters of data.
Retention: YoY retention improved; a separate task force targets repeat business; plans to be announced in the next call if finalised this month.
Marketing will shift from top-of-mind branding to consideration and conversion-led social campaigns for Q3.

qa_highlights.answer: Break-even-type benchmarks: about INR7,000/sq ft (Tier 3), INR8,500 (Tier 2), INR10,000-10,500 (Tier 1). Management said franchisee ROI is good and there is no pressure.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said competition has never been a closure reason. Closures were from market shifts, cannibalisation by larger nearby stores, and early mistakes. Q1 was front-loaded to avoid off-season rentals.

qa_highlights.answer: GM was 65.7% in Q1 FY27 versus 65.0% in Q4 FY26, so it improved sequentially. GST was not in the base in Q1 and entered the base from Q3, which explains YoY comparisons.

qa_highlights.question: Primary vs secondary sales gap despite Adhik maas impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Replenishment is auto-driven, so quarterly gaps vary. Management asked analysts to review primary and secondary at full-year level, where directions align.

qa_highlights.question: Inventory days?
qa_highlights.answer: 34 days for TTM June 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Plans for revenue growth of low-to-mid teens, and how to fund square footage addition?

qa_highlights.question: Is Mohey scaling and what are the steps?
qa_highlights.answer: Mohey performing better than company average; doubling down on non-bridal categories (stitched suits, sarees, crop-top lehengas) and digital marketing for them.

qa_highlights.question: Share of MBO, SIS and e-commerce in revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: About 5% combined today, with aggressive growth targets.

543470|2026-03.headline: Softtech Q4 FY26 revenue rose 50% YoY to INR 46.6 crore and FY26 revenue hit INR 132.9 crore, with management targeting INR 300 crore by FY29.

FY26 revenue was INR 132.9 crore (up 40%), EBITDA INR 32.2 crore (24% margin) and PAT INR 5.3 crore. Management highlighted the TDR exchange mandate in Mumbai (BMC), an Airport Authority of India mandate, first CivitSUSTAIN order, and early German and US traction. Order book is about INR 232 crore against a pipeline of about INR 436 crore. This was the company's maiden earnings call.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR 0.5 crore in Q4 FY25; +113% QoQ
vs INR 0.1 crore in Q4 FY25; +133% QoQ

segments.commentary: About 50% of FY26 revenue; management expects the same share in FY27, possibly higher due to transaction-based projects going live. Penetration cited at 1,500+ cities and 18 states.

segments.name: CivitINFRA
segments.commentary: About 25% of FY26 revenue; expected to be flat or slightly lower in FY27. Airport Authority of India order of INR 16-17 crore (incl. GST) is a one-time licence, with about 40% recognised in FY26 and the balance over about three years.

segments.name: CivitBUILD, BIM/GIS services and others
segments.commentary: Together about 15-20% of revenue. CivitBUILD has won private construction-enterprise projects; Middle East and African work exists.

qa_highlights.answer: Order book about INR 200-odd crore, about 60% to be booked this year, roughly 40% of that recurring. Pipeline conversion probability is above 60%.

qa_highlights.question: Details of the CivitSUSTAIN order with Mitsubishi and the GIFT City pipeline?

543482|2026-03.headline: Eureka Forbes Q4 FY26 revenue rose 11.6% YoY to INR 684 crore with record 13.2% adjusted EBITDA margin; FY27 margins guided to hold.

543482|2026-06.headline: Eureka Forbes Q1 FY27 revenue rose 15.3% YoY to INR701 crore, but adjusted EBITDA margin fell 46 bps to 10.5% on a 131 bps gross margin drop.

Adjusted EBITDA rose 10.5% to INR74 crore, but margin slipped 46 bps to 10.5% as gross margin fell 131 bps to 58.4% and A&SP spend was front-loaded. Service revenue growth was similar to Q4 FY26, while AMC bookings softened after price increases of roughly 3% to 12%. Management guided to a clear step-up in full-year growth and to FY27 EBITDA margins broadly in line with FY26.

segments.commentary: Grew late teens, broad-based across retail, direct and e-commerce, each with strong double-digit growth.

segments.name: Emerging categories (robotics, softeners, air purifiers)
segments.commentary: Strong growth across all emerging categories; robotics driven by premium mix (fully automatic cleaning station), softeners by volume. Robotics campaign launched with Shraddha Kapoor.

qa_highlights.answer: Growth was mainly volume-led for water and softeners, while robotics growth came from premium mix. Pricing had some impact in water; management did not quantify it.

qa_highlights.answer: Yes, it helps FY27 revenue. However, in-year bookings must sustain growth, and the softness in AMC bookings is expected to show more in the later part of the year. Q2 service growth is expected to be similar to Q1.

qa_highlights.answer: Management expects products and emerging categories to grow faster than services, with filters growing ahead of AMC. It reaffirmed 2x revenue vs FY25 (about 17-18% CAGR) and 3x EBITDA by FY30.

543498|2026-09.headline: MSWIL Q2 FY27 revenue rose 47% YoY to a strong quarter, with EBITDA margin at 9.2% (up from 7.6% in Q1) despite copper and wage headwinds.
543498|2026-09.overview: Management reported revenue up 47% YoY and 19% QoQ, EBITDA up 34% YoY and 45% QoQ, and PAT up 35% YoY and 54% QoQ, growing ahead of the passenger vehicle industry (volumes +25% YoY, +14% QoQ). The three Greenfield plants (Kharkhauda, Gujarat, Pune) have ramped to optimal utilisation and are now treated as part of the regular network. Copper, up about 54% YoY and 6% QoQ, is a pass-through with a roughly three-month recovery lag, and minimum wage revisions remain a cost headwind. Management guided to continued industry growth in H2 but with a narrower percentage range because of a higher base after last year's GST cut, and gave FY27 capex of about Rs 200 crore with no FY28 figure yet.

qa_highlights.answer: Management expects continued growth and ongoing programme launches, though Q3 is seasonally offset by the Shradh period and percentage growth will be narrower than last year.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the gross margin decline and the improvement in other operating costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management linked the gross margin pressure to copper and wage costs under negotiation with customers, with recovery expected within FY27. Lower other operating costs were attributed to Greenfield revenue ramp and austerity measures; no forward guidance was given.

qa_highlights.question: How much copper under-recovery is left if prices stay at Q2 levels?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the lag is mostly one quarter (up to six months in some cases) and that prices have not stabilised, so the residual could not be quantified; over time, it said, buy and sell prices equalise.

qa_highlights.question: Does zonal architecture reduce content per vehicle, and how much growth is at risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Management argued content growth comes from innovation and premiumisation, not only architecture, and said the harness has 7-8 million components with customer-specific designs, so full in-house supply is not feasible.

qa_highlights.question: What are the normalised gross margins versus FY24 to FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to guide on margins, pointing to ROCE and saying pass-through would lift the numerator and denominator together, so reported percentages may look lower even if returns are healthy.

qa_highlights.question: What is current capacity utilisation and FY27/FY28 capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Expansion is triggered at about 80% utilisation; FY27 capex is about Rs 200 crore and FY28 is not yet quantifiable.

qa_highlights.question: Why has revenue growth outpaced EBITDA growth?

543514|2026-03.headline: Veranda FY26 revenue rose 35% to INR 482 crore and PAT turned positive at INR 130 crore; FY27 guidance is INR 670 crore revenue and INR 144 crore PAT.
543514|2026-03.overview: Management reported Q4 FY26 revenue of INR 132 crore (up 52% YoY) and FY26 EBITDA of about INR 204 crore (up 135%). FY26 PAT of INR 130 crore compares with a loss of about INR 252 crore in FY25, and this was the fifth consecutive PAT-positive quarter. Management said FY26 guidance was broadly achieved, with non-commerce well ahead and commerce broadly in line. The J.K. Shah Commerce Education demerger is awaiting final NCLT approval, with listing targeted for end-July or mid-August 2026. FY27 guidance is revenue of about INR 670 crore and PAT above INR 144 crore.

segments.commentary: Significantly outperformed estimates on government test prep traction and operational improvements. Government test prep posted a Q4 loss of about INR 3 crore after a one-time INR 5 crore impairment; the segment otherwise earned INR 2 crore EBITDA for the year.

Academic segment: evaluating managed pre-KG schools and expanding managed K-12 schools.

qa_highlights.question: When will the J.K. Shah demerger list, and how will the listing unlock value?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the NCLT hearing is on June 3, 2026, with the final order about 30 days later, then ROC filings and listing approvals; listing is expected by end-July or mid-August 2026. Management said the standalone commerce business is sharply focused and expected to carry a higher valuation multiple.

qa_highlights.question: Why does a vocational-division revenue of INR 51 crore still appear in consolidated results?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said one North American entity was not hived off with the divestment and remains with the non-commerce business; it is planned for eventual sale subject to RBI approvals.

qa_highlights.question: Why was there a Q4 loss in government test prep, and are there further impairments?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said a one-time INR 5 crore impairment was taken in Q4 following audit testing; the segment otherwise earned INR 2 crore EBITDA for the year. Management said goodwill and intangibles were tested and no further impairment was taken in FY26.

qa_highlights.question: How will the warrants issued for the BB Virtuals and Navkar acquisitions be treated on demerger?
qa_highlights.answer: About 75% of the warrants are yet to be subscribed, with the deadline in August 2026. If demerger happens before then, warrants will be split proportionately between the two entities on the same asset ratio, per the scheme.

qa_highlights.question: Why will FY27 commerce EBITDA margin dip about 4-5%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the dip to front-loaded opex for about 15 new colleges. Lease deposits and soft capex are capitalised in year one, while faculty and marketing are expensed; the first year is expected to be marginally breakeven, with benefits from year two.

qa_highlights.question: What is the reinvestment plan for surplus cash after debt repayment and demerger?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said cash will fund commerce geographic expansion across all districts and new products including 11th-12th education, and non-commerce expansion in Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh and Telangana, plus managed pre-KG and K-12 schools.

Mumbai (Malad): no precise margin given; EBITDA margins should eventually exceed 20%. Core doctors to stay full-time, with hybrid model possible for some specialty doctors.
key_quotes: we remain confident of delivering revenue growth in the 20% range during the second quarter as well. We expect growth to remain above 20%.

I am not in a position to provide a precise margin expectation today. However, I am confident that EBITDA margins should eventually be above 20%, although it is too early to estimate where they will ultimately stabilize.
We continue to expect EBITDA margins to return to the 24% –25% range on a pre -Ind AS basis by the end of the year.

543524|2026-09.headline: Q2 FY27 revenue rose 23.2% YoY to INR 548 crore, but EBITDA grew only 14.2% to INR 170 crore (31% margin) as new-hospital losses and marketing spend weighed.
543524|2026-09.overview: Rainbow Children's Medicare reported Q2 FY27 operating revenue of INR 548 crore (+23.2% YoY), EBITDA of INR 170 crore (+14.2%, 31% margin) and PAT of INR 83.9 crore (+10.9%). H1 revenue was INR 1,018 crore (+27.6%) with H1 EBITDA of INR 304.6 crore (+20.6%, 29.9% margin). Patient consultations, deliveries and inpatient discharges grew 19%, 20% and 15% YoY in the quarter, with a soft monsoon and little seasonal benefit. The company opened a 70-bed Nellore and 50-bed Guntur hospital, and management reiterated a large pipeline of roughly 1,050 beds under construction plus a Delhi NCR hub and a 2,300-bed addition over three years.

segments.name: Mature hospitals (>5 years old)

segments.name: Emerging hospitals
segments.commentary: Margins described as healthy and broadly in line with mature hospitals despite lower occupancy; no specific figure was disclosed on the call.

segments.name: New hospitals (commenced in last 6-8 months)
segments.commentary: EBITDA margin around negative 16% per management. Rajahmundry and Mahadevapura (Bengaluru) reached operational breakeven; HRBR Electronic City and other Bengaluru hospitals are nearing breakeven.

segments.name: IVF / fertility
segments.commentary: Contributes about 5% of revenue (up from about 3% in the prior-year quarter), mostly in-house via obstetrics OPD conversion plus 2-3 standalone centres; management declined to disclose segment margins.

guidance_outlook: Revenue growth expectation stated as high-teens, with management optimistic about higher; earlier guided ~20% revenue CAGR.
ARPOB growth normally 7-8%; ARPP growth averages 6-7% over three years.
Pre-Ind AS EBITDA margin threshold of around 25-26% maintained as the network expands; post-Ind AS margin around 30-31%.
Possible margin pressure of about 0.5% in a quarter when many beds are added, and 0.5-1% for a few quarters with Delhi NCR launch.
New hospitals targeted to reach EBITDA breakeven within two years; Hyderabad about 1 year, Bengaluru 12-15 months, Chennai 15-18 months.
HIS rollout expected to complete in about 4 months; new website and patient app to launch in the next few months.
capex_capacity: Indore clinical operations expected in Q3 FY27; adjacent 120-bed greenfield groundbreaking on Diwali date.

NCR Gurugram: 125-bed Sector 56 ready in Q3 FY28; 325-bed Sector 44 hub hospital for clinical operations in Q1 FY29.
100-bed Seegehalli (Bengaluru) spoke and 150-bed Pune greenfield in early construction, likely ready in 2H FY29.

Amaravati pediatric hospital planned in two phases, initial capacity 150 beds on 2 acres allotted by Andhra Pradesh government. Chennai project delayed about six months due to re-approvals, now back on track.
About 1,050 beds under construction; about 2,300 beds to be added over the next three years; network currently about 2,600 beds (5,000+ target).

Pharmacy costs about 14% of net revenue; about 7% is vaccinations and under 0.5% is oncology/drugs potentially under price caps, so management sees the oncology price-cap impact as insignificant (under 0.5% EBITDA margin compression).
Management says growth initiatives are about 50-60% complete over a 1.5-2 year roadmap; competition from Cloudnine, Kids Clinic and Motherhood seen as limited, mainly in obstetrics.
M&A limited to paediatric-compatible assets; highest acquisition multiple paid was about 11x EV/EBITDA.

qa_highlights.question: How will new-bed additions in new cities affect margins, and will there be annual pressure?

qa_highlights.question: What is the right metric (ARPOB vs ARPP) and what headroom exists?

qa_highlights.question: What is the maximum achievable occupancy and when will the mature-hospital target be reached?

qa_highlights.question: What execution risk comes with entering many new cities?

qa_highlights.question: Will the oncology drug price cap affect Rainbow?
qa_highlights.answer: Pharmacy 14% of net revenue; vaccinations about 7% (not capped); remaining 7% has under 0.5% oncology/price-cap exposure. Impact deemed insignificant.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Delhi NCR hub and expansion sustain 25-26% pre-Ind AS margins, and what are M&A plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects 0.5-1% margin pressure for a few quarters with NCR; phased launch to limit losses; breakeven targeted within two years. M&A opportunities exist but are limited; no share of the 1,100 beds from M&A quantified.

risks_watch: EBITDA growth (14%) lagging revenue growth (23%) as marketing spend and new-hospital losses (about -16% margin) rise; track margin trend vs 25-26% pre-Ind AS threshold.
Delhi NCR launch (Gurugram Sector 44 hub, Q1 FY29) and Delhi losses in FY29-FY30; breakeven guidance to be given 3-6 months before launch.

Occupancy in mature hospitals (about 54%) versus 60% ceiling; seasonal benefit absent in last three quarters.
Growth from high-teens guidance versus 20%+ recent run-rate; IVF and obstetrics mix shift.

543526|2026-03.headline: LIC FY26 net VNB rose 41.63% to ₹14,179 crore, with VNB margin up 360 bps to 21.2% on non-par mix and economic assumptions.
543526|2026-03.overview: LIC reported record FY26 PAT of ₹57,419 crore (up 19.25% YoY) and net VNB of ₹14,179 crore (up 41.63%), with margin at 21.2% versus 17.6%. Non-par share of individual APE rose to 35.11% from 27.69% a year earlier, and the solvency ratio improved to 2.35 from 2.11. Embedded value grew only 1.58% to ₹7,89,185 crore because of ₹1.00 lakh crore-plus of equity and debt MTM declines in the year. Management flagged upcoming risk-based capital (RBC) rules as the reason it is cautious on dividend payout, even after raising the final dividend to ₹20 per share pre-bonus.

segments.name: Individual business
segments.commentary: Individual APE ₹43,335 crore; non-par APE rose 43.78% to ₹15,214 crore, 35.11% of individual APE. Individual market share fell to 36.6% from 37.46%.

segments.name: Group business
segments.commentary: Group premium ₹1,96,609 crore (+16.26%); group APE ₹23,626 crore. Group market share 70.11% vs 71.19%. Group contributed about 19% of VNB per the Appointed Actuary's breakdown.

segments.name: Bancassurance and alternate channels
segments.commentary: NBP ₹5,076 crore (+45.19%): banks ₹3,151 crore (+22.30%), alternate channels ₹1,925 crore (+109.36%). Share of individual NBP 7.51% vs 5.59%. Policy count fell sharply, which management attributed to a microfinance corporate agency issue.

segments.name: Agency channel
segments.commentary: Agency sourced 91.75% of new business premium and 98.42% of policies. Individual agents fell to 14,57,045 from 14,86,851.

guidance_outlook: No formal numeric guidance. Management expects VNB margin to keep improving, driven by higher ticket size and better persistency, but said further expansion will be gradual and slower from here.
Management said it is not looking for major changes in the business mix from here and aims to consolidate, with VNB growth coming from either margin or volume.
Management said maturity outgo will stay high through January 2027 from 25-year-old Jeevan Shree-type assured-benefit policies.
Dividend payout policy will be finalised only after RBC outcomes are clear; management expects the increased payout to be sustained.
April 2026 sales were described as good, ahead of the prior year, across participating and non-participating products.
risks_watch: RBC framework timing and calibration, which is likely to be equity-sensitive and could constrain capital and payout.
Equity and debt MTM volatility: ₹53,698 crore equity and ₹46,853 crore debt fall in FY26 hit EV growth (only +1.58%).
Persistency on a premium basis softened in the 13th and 25th months, and the 61st-month figure fell to 59.31% from 63.12%. The positive persistency variance (₹3,509 crore) may not repeat.
Margin sustainability: the GST charge, RFR tailwind and mix benefit may not recur, and management said margin could be challenged in the next three years.
Agent count down to 14,57,045 from 14,86,851, and bancassurance policy count down about 36%.
Upcoming Ind AS/IFRS transition and its effect on VIF-to-CSM translation, which is still being worked on.
Heavy maturity outgo through January 2027 from high sum assured legacy policies.
543526|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on headline growth (VNB, margin, PAT, bancassurance), but noticeably cautious on dividend policy and margin outlook, deferring to RBC clarity. Evasive on the FY27 margin level and product-level IRR questions.
key_quotes: We are now very confident that having achieved significant directional changes, we are now on a path of superior growth with sharper focus on enhanced performance parameters.
We do not want to create expectations which cannot be sustainable for future, as a responsible organization, we would like how the RBC pans out.
This journey possibly can be very gradual and slow from here because we have seen even for the industry, the margins have been around between 20s to maximum 30s for a very short period of time.
This is the highest PAT in our history.

qa_highlights.question: Which products drove the non-par individual savings growth in Q4, and how much of that momentum continues into FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Uthup Joseph said savings bucket grew about 48.40%, led by Jeevan Utsav on ticket size; Jeevan Labh contributed about 40% of par savings premium. No FY27 momentum figure was given.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the VNB margin bridge from 17.6% to 21.2%, and what were the operating assumption and EV walk items?
qa_highlights.answer: A.K. Srivastava: business mix +3%, RFR +3.4%, operating assumption changes including GST -2.8%. EV walk: unwind ₹74,748 crore, operating assumption changes -₹1,663 crore, operating experience variance +₹92,639 crore, equity MTM -₹53,698 crore, debt MTM -₹46,853 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the operating variance positive for several years, and what is the persistency variance breakup?
qa_highlights.answer: Persistency variance +₹3,509 crore, largely from participating and group business; par 13th-month persistency improved (+₹2,463 crore). Group persistency assumption was strengthened. Expense variance positive net of GST; mortality roughly flat.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the solvency-driven dividend payout cautious even with solvency at 2.35, and how should the payout ratio be viewed?
qa_highlights.answer: Dinesh Pant said the company wants clarity on RBC because equity exposure is high, and it does not want to create expectations it cannot sustain; growth also consumes capital. Doraiswamy said the payout will depend on regulation, with the increased payout (₹20 per share pre-bonus) expected to be sustained.

qa_highlights.question: Will non-par IRRs or offering rates be revised in FY27, and why did bancassurance policy count fall about 36%?
qa_highlights.answer: Pant said IRRs depend on investment opportunities, competition and margin balance; hedging for long-duration non-par is limited. Hemant Buch attributed the bancassurance policy decline to one microfinance corporate agency issue and a conscious move to bigger tickets; Q4 sales count rose about 10%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin outlook for the next year and the building blocks for expansion from here?
qa_highlights.answer: Pant said margins could be challenged over the next three years and the journey will be gradual; the company will not chase margins at the cost of insurance-for-all. Doraiswamy said ticket size and persistency are the drivers, with product mix to consolidate.

capex_capacity: No capex, capacity or commissioning discussion on the call; the call covered insurance sales, margins, capital and dividend.
