Digital capacity: 23,00,983 policies completed via the agent-assisted ANANDA app in FY26 vs 14,74,208 in FY25 (+56.08%); active agents on ANANDA up 29.56%. New MyLIC customer app launched (15 April 2026) and LIC Super Sales Saathi app for sales personnel under the DIVE programme.
Bima Sakhi scheme: 3,45,000 Bima Sakhis appointed, 21.94 lakh policies sold and ₹2,848 crore new business premium in FY26; coverage at 1,43,924 of 2,44,876 Gram Panchayats (59%).
demand_pricing: Market share by first-year premium 56.6% in FY26 vs 57.05% in FY25; individual market share 36.6% (vs 37.46%); group 70.11% (vs 71.19%).
Individual new business premium ₹67,676 crore (+8.29%); individual renewal premium ₹2,71,699 crore (+5.91%); group new business premium ₹1,92,912 crore out of group total ₹1,96,609 crore (+16.26%).

Non-par individual APE ₹15,214 crore (+43.78%), 35.11% of individual APE vs 27.69%. Jeevan Utsav was the main contributor to savings growth (management cited ~48.40% savings bucket growth); Jeevan Labh contributed about 40% of par savings premium.

VNB margin bridge 17.6% to 21.2%: business mix +3%, RFR +3.4%, operating assumption changes (expense and persistency realignment plus GST) -2.8%. Individual par ~42% of APE contributes ~28% of VNB; individual non-par ~22.7% of APE contributes ~53% of VNB; remainder group (~19%).

Operating experience variance of ₹92,639 crore; persistency variance +₹3,509 crore (group line strengthened, par 13th-month persistency improved, +₹2,463 crore); mortality roughly flat; expense variance positive, net of GST.

Economic variance: equity MTM fall ₹53,698 crore and debt MTM fall ₹46,853 crore. Bond-amortisation accounting change impact of about ₹11,000 crore gross, of which ~₹9,000 crore sits in participating business (no direct PAT impact per management).

Bancassurance and alternate channels NBP ₹5,076 crore (+45.19%): banks ₹3,151 crore (+22.30%), alternate channels ₹1,925 crore (+109.36%). Policy count via bancassurance fell about 36%; management attributed this to a microfinance corporate agency issue and a conscious move away from login-based low-ticket sales; Q4 policy count reportedly up ~10%.

Agency: individual agents 14,57,045 vs 14,86,851 (down ~30,000); agency sourced 98.42% of policies and 91.75% of new business premium. Management said recruitment, training and younger-age agent focus will follow.

April 2026 sales described as good and ahead of FY26 pace across participating and non-participating products; management said it is too early to judge the effect of recent market volatility on ULIP and guaranteed demand.
Pricing: management said non-par IRRs depend on investment opportunities and competition and are balanced against margins; long-duration hedges are limited. Expense ratio 11.91% (-51 bps).

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: VNB margin rose 360 bps to 21.2% in FY26, but management says further expansion will be gradual and slower, and the bridge included a one-off RFR (+3.4%) and GST-related assumption charge (-2.8%) that may not recur; margin 'could be challenged over the next three years'.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Individual NBP grew only 8.29% to ₹67,676 crore and market share slipped to 56.6% from 57.05%; April 2026 sales described as good and ahead of prior year, but agent count fell to 14,57,045 from 14,86,851 and bancassurance policy count fell about 36%.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: No capex, capacity or commissioning discussed; solvency rose to 2.35 from 2.11 and management is building reserves ahead of RBC, so capital is being retained rather than deployed into new capacity.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: No numeric guidance; management is cautious on margin outlook and says it is not looking for major mix changes, aiming to consolidate.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Positive FY26 operating variance of ₹92,639 crore and persistency variance of ₹3,509 crore may not repeat, and RBC rules (equity-sensitive) could constrain capital and payout, with EV growth only 1.58% after ₹1 lakh crore-plus MTM hits.

rows.label: Dividend payout increase pending RBC clarity
rows.why: Final dividend raised to ₹20 per share pre-bonus and management expects the higher payout to be sustained, but finality is deferred until RBC outcomes are clear and solvency is 2.35.

rows.label: RBC framework timing and calibration
rows.why: Management explicitly flagged upcoming RBC rules as the reason for caution on payout and capital, with equity exposure high and the framework's calibration still unknown.

rows.label: Bancassurance and alternate channel momentum
rows.why: Bancassurance and alternate channels NBP rose 45.19% to ₹5,076 crore, with alternate channels up 109.36%, though bancassurance policy count fell about 36% and Q4 policy count was up about 10%.

tone.note: Management was confident on VNB, margin, PAT and bancassurance growth and on the 2.35 solvency ratio, but cautious on dividend payout and the gradual margin outlook pending RBC clarity; analysts pressed on FY27 IRRs, persistency and the sustainability of margin gains.

543526|2026-06.headline: LIC Q1 FY27 net VNB margin rose 750 bps YoY to 22.9% and VNB grew 61.32% to ₹3,136 crore; profit after tax up 22.81% to ₹13,492 crore.
543526|2026-06.overview: LIC reported Q1 FY27 (quarter ended 30 June 2026) with total premium of ₹127,250 crore (+6.75% YoY) and individual new business premium of ₹14,351 crore (+14.48% YoY). Net VNB margin expanded to 22.9% from 15.4%, driven mainly by business mix (non-par savings and protection growth) and a 2.9% positive assumption impact, partly offset by a 1.9% negative expense impact from loss of GST input tax credit. Overall market share by first-year premium fell to 60.10% from 63.51%, with group share down to 70.90% and individual share up to 38.89%. The company also disclosed the 6.5% government OFS, taking public float to 10%.

segments.name: Individual business
segments.commentary: Individual new business premium ₹14,351 crore (+14.48%); individual renewal premium ₹61,065 crore (+3.61%); individual APE ₹7,532 crore with non-par share rising to 32.49% from 30.34%. ULIP premium declined YoY.

segments.name: Group business
segments.commentary: Group total premium ₹51,834 crore (+8.61%); group APE ₹6,160 crore; group market share fell to 70.90% from 76.54% on a comparable basis.

segments.name: Par vs non-par (APE)
segments.commentary: Par individual APE ₹5,085 crore (67.51% of individual APE); non-par ₹2,447 crore (32.49%). Management cited non-par savings growth of 59.24% and non-par protection growth of 43.59%.

segments.name: Bancassurance and alternate channels
segments.commentary: NBP ₹907.14 crore (+5.25%); bank channel NBP ₹483.39 crore (-8.62%) due to delayed bank marketing plans and West Asia related remittance pressure on annuities; alternate channels ₹423.75 crore (+27.27%).

capex_capacity: The call did not discuss capex, capacity, utilisation, or commissioning timelines; no capex plans were stated.

Product pipeline: two new products launched since April 2026 (New Jeevan Sathi single premium and limited premium); Nav Jeevan Shree single premium withdrawn. Total of 59 products available for new business as of 30 June 2026.

Digital and distribution capacity: MyLIC and Super Sales Saathi apps launched in April 2026 under the DIVE initiative; agent-assisted Ananda application completed 436,925 policies in Q1 FY27 (+25.56% YoY).
Bima Sakhi rollout: 2.87 lakh women designated, covering 151,620 of 244,876 gram panchayats (62%) as of 30 June 2026; target is at least one Bima Sakhi per gram panchayat.
Agent force: 1,445,692 agents as of 30 June 2026 (-2.73% YoY); management said non-serious Bima Sakhi recruits are being weeded out, which will continue.
guidance_outlook: Management does not normally give guidance but expects VNB margin to keep improving over the next few quarters, subject to RFR movements.
Management said VNB margin should settle around the industry average and is working toward mid-20s VNB margin by year end.
Non-par growth expected to continue from Q1 to Q4 pattern; ULIP recovery expected when market normalises.
Expense ratio expected to fall with operational efficiency; GST ITC-related expense impact to be compared against last year in Q1 and Q2 only.
Bancassurance expected to recover in subsequent quarters after delayed bank marketing plans.
APE growth expected to strengthen in subsequent quarters as new business focus increases through the year.
demand_pricing: Individual protection growth above 40% YoY on a small base; individual agents drove most protection policy volume.
ULIP premium declined YoY due to market volatility; management said it expects recovery only when markets normalise and denied cannibalisation of non-par.
Average ticket size rose after minimum sum assured for the major regular-premium product was raised from ₹1 lakh to ₹2 lakh (October 2024) and annuity single-premium sales grew.

Renewal commission growth declined YoY, attributed to agents no longer in the books and not eligible to renew commission.

qa_highlights.question: What are the assumption changes in the VNB walk and is the cost impact GST-led?
qa_highlights.answer: Assumption changes contributed +2.9% (RFR, persistency alignment, CRNHR, TVOG); expense assumptions including loss of ITC contributed -1.9%. Business mix contributed about +6.5%. The GST exemption removed ITC, adding to expenses, but higher volumes should dilute per-policy expenses.

qa_highlights.question: Is the ULIP decline deliberate and will it recover in Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Mainly market-driven due to volatility; management focused on margin-accretive non-par lines. ULIP recovery depends on market improvement; no cannibalisation expected.

qa_highlights.question: Why does RWRP differ from individual APE?
qa_highlights.answer: APE annualises new business premium by frequency and excludes first-year renewal premiums received after policy completion; RWRP captures actual premium received, so the gap reflects strong first-year renewal premium.

qa_highlights.question: Why is APE growth soft despite strong VNB growth, and what is the medium-term aspiration?
qa_highlights.answer: Prior-year base had higher regular-premium share; management expects APE growth to pick up in later quarters. No numeric medium-term target given; management agreed to examine monthly APE disclosure.

qa_highlights.question: Split of VNB margin by line of business?
qa_highlights.answer: Par: 37.1% of APE with 19.4% margin; individual non-par: ₹1,678 crore APE with 49.3% margin; group: 45% of APE with 29.4% margin (figures given as shares of VNB as well as APE by the Appointed Actuary, clarified as proportion of VNB by segment).

qa_highlights.question: Why is the solvency ratio high and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: 2.42 is pre-dividend; 2.32 after subsequent dividend. Higher solvency supports protection growth, but management will await regulatory changes before deciding on any change to solvency strategy.

qa_highlights.question: Why is bancassurance individual NBP growing much slower than policy count?
qa_highlights.answer: Bank channel faced pressure from West Asia conflict affecting remittances (annuities) and market volatility (ULIPs); low-ticket policies were withdrawn after minimum sum assured rose to ₹2 lakh.

qa_highlights.question: Is VNB margin on track for mid-20s by year end?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is working toward that target.

risks_watch: Assumption and RFR movements: RFR contributed positively, but management said it is outside LIC's control and could change the margin trajectory.
Persistency weakness: 61-month premium persistency fell to 61.12% from 63.85%; 13-month number-based persistency rose to 66.45% from 64.35%; group persistency contributed negatively to assumptions.
Market share erosion: overall first-year premium share fell to 60.10% from 63.51%; group share fell sharply.
Expense ratio up 16 bps YoY to 10.63% after loss of GST input tax credit; volume growth must outpace expense growth.
Maturity claims up 12.88% YoY to ₹57,099 crore; agent count down 2.73% YoY.
Bancassurance bank channel NBP down 8.62%; recovery timing uncertain.
Solvency pre-dividend 2.42, post-dividend 2.32; any capital needs for protection growth require monitoring.
Shareholder profit from ASM funds (₹180,000 crore book value) and par surplus transfer timing (mainly Q4) affect quarterly profit comparisons.
IEV unwind and EV not disclosed quarterly; next disclosure at half-year.

543527|2026-03.headline: Prudent Q4 FY26: record ₹4,300 crore quarterly equity net sales offset MTM hit; AUM rebounded to ₹1.33 trillion by 5 May 2026.
543527|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 average AUM rose 0.3% QoQ to ₹1,28,000 crore and 26% YoY despite a 14.5% market fall, helped by record quarterly equity net sales of ₹4,300 crore. Closing equity AUM fell 8.2% QoQ to ₹1,15,480 crore on ₹14,550 crore of mark-to-market losses. Revenue grew 5.1% QoQ and operating profit 19.5% QoQ, but PAT growth slowed to 2.6% QoQ because other income turned negative (₹-4.7 crore). Management flagged two regulatory items for FY27: SEBI's TER change (GST now inside the expense ratio) and withdrawal of the 5 bps exit-load benefit, with industry clarity expected by end-May.

In line with 21.7% average AUM growth; yield stable at 91 bps

qa_highlights.question: Why was the fee and commission expense ratio lower in Q4, and is it Indus-driven?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to a nil additional trail provision in Q4 (₹5.5 crore in Q3) plus about ₹4.5 crore of insurance revenue recognised in March, about ₹10 crore extra revenue in total. Full-year commission figures were said to be more representative.

qa_highlights.question: How will the exit-load pass-on and GST-driven TER change affect distributor payouts and yields?
qa_highlights.answer: New business yield expected broadly neutral; book impact 2-3 bps, pending clarity from a couple of AMCs. Payouts will be realigned net of GST, with the April calculation still pending, so the monetary impact cannot yet be quantified.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 'lump sum' share of flows persist if markets recover?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said lump sum is typically higher in corrections and the long-run mix is around 50:50; a market downturn would shift mix toward SIPs over time.

qa_highlights.question: Is SIP market share (3.5-3.7%) being lost to other platforms or direct?
qa_highlights.answer: Direct share is rising industry-wide. Prudent says it is gaining regular-plan share and rising monthly by a few bps, but it does not target a specific share level.

qa_highlights.question: What share of MFD AUM is held by larger distributors, and does leakage occur after scale?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave no AUM share; 2,220 MFDs have crossed ₹10 crore AUM. No MFD has left after reaching ₹100 crore, per management; 40-50% of joiners are new to the industry.

qa_highlights.question: Indus AUM retention and further acquisitions?
qa_highlights.answer: Indus AUM has grown from ₹2,060 crore (Sept 2025) to ₹2,250 crore with the full team retained. Further acquisitions are being scouted but nothing is concrete.

543527|2026-06.headline: Prudent's Q1 FY27 PAT rose 44.4% YoY to INR74.8 crores, with average AUM up 21% to INR1.33 lakh crores despite a 2.8 bps gross yield cut.
543527|2026-06.overview: Prudent reported Q1 FY27 with average AUM of INR1.33 lakh crores (up 21% YoY, 4% QoQ) and equity AUM of INR1.34 lakh crores as of June 2026. Operating profit rose 32.4% YoY to INR89.1 crores and PAT rose 44.4% YoY to INR74.8 crores, helped by treasury gains. New SEBI/AMC regulatory changes from April 2026 (GST treatment, exit load removal) cut gross yield by about 2.8 bps to around 88 bps and shifted commission expense lower, which management called a one-time reset. Management said the current margin should be the run-rate for the next three quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What was the gross margin last quarter and how has it moved this quarter, and what is the standalone MF contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanjay Shah said MF margin was 91.2 bps last quarter and about 88.4 bps this quarter, a 2.8 bps fall due to the 5 bps exit load removal from TER. Segment margins are not disclosed; operating margin is the suggested proxy.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Q1 commission-to-revenue ratio (56.2% standalone) a steady-state number?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanjay Shah said the current margin can be used for the next three quarters and the spread should hold, as the regulatory changes were applied across the full book. Shirish Patel added that insurance mix in Q4 was higher, which also affects the ratio.

qa_highlights.question: What is the net revenue yield after commissions and will it persist?
qa_highlights.answer: Shirish Patel said current yield levels would likely persist in the near term; medium to long term it could fall 1 to 2 bps, mainly on new business.

qa_highlights.question: Can MFD partners go direct once mutual-fund-only PMS is allowed?
qa_highlights.answer: Shirish Patel said the risk is low since MFDs need a platform; a possible consolidation of licences is the bigger effect. No yield uplift is assumed from the 2.25% PMS fee structure.

qa_highlights.question: Who are the new MFD additions and what is the direct versus indirect AUM split?

qa_highlights.question: How should AUM growth be viewed beyond MTM, and how fast is net sales growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Shirish Patel said net sales historically add about 10-12% to AUM each year, and FY26 growth came mainly from net sales rather than MTM.

543527|2026-09.headline: Q2 FY27 equity AUM rose 1.7% QoQ to INR1.37 lakh crore despite INR1,867 crore MTM drag, with record INR4,137 crore net sales.
543527|2026-09.overview: Quarterly average AUM reached INR1.43 lakh crore, up 8% QoQ and 21% YoY, while revenue from operations rose 11.8% QoQ and operating profit rose 15.4% QoQ with margin expanding 80 bps to 26.4%. Reported PAT fell 4.1% QoQ to INR71.7 crore because other income dropped about 82% to INR3.8 crore on bond-yield and hybrid-portfolio mark-to-market reversals. Management said the sharp market correction in late October leaves current AUM slightly below the first-half average of INR1.38 lakh crore. The bulk of the call went to a proposed insurance distribution regulation (IDA vs IDE commission gap), where management said insurance is about 12% of PBT and the impact is uncertain.

segments.name: Mutual fund distribution
segments.commentary: Quarterly average AUM up 8% QoQ; MF yield stable at 88-89 bps. Equity AUM share ex-ETF rose from 2.59% to 2.7% YoY; SIP market share rose from 3.49% to 3.73%.

segments.name: Insurance distribution
segments.commentary: Insurance revenue up 35% QoQ; general insurance fresh premium up 54% QoQ and 62% YoY; life fresh premium up 37% QoQ and 45% YoY. Management puts the insurance contribution at about 12% of profit (PBT).

segments.name: Other financial and non-financial products (incl. PMS)
segments.commentary: Revenue up 14% QoQ, led by PMS distribution; average PMS AUM grew 37% YoY to about INR2,020 crore.

guidance_outlook: Management expects MF PMS framework to be operational from April 2027; company is applying for MF PMS license via subsidiary renamed Prudent Asset Management Private Limited (formerly Prutech).

Management said that if the insurance proposal were implemented as drafted (IDE renewal commission 5% vs 10% for IDA), it would hurt the insurance business, but called that scenario unlikely; the final regulation is awaited before giving numbers.
Management expects renewal commission cuts to be passed on to POSPs from April onwards, reducing absolute margin on that book.
Company is awaiting SEBI's final FICP framework before launching online bond distribution through its OBPP license.
capex_capacity: Pan-India branch network and tech platform; around 700 sales employees cited as capacity to support distributors moving into MF.
SIF certification: 1,792 distributors certified; SIF AUM nearly INR900 crore.
Onboarded about 3,541 new distributors in H1 FY27, nearly 30% higher than H1 FY26.
demand_pricing: Industry net sales were weak; Prudent's net sales were the highest ever. Management says redemptions are lower than before and SIP cancellations rose.
SIP contributes about 50% of Prudent's gross sales; management said its market-share gains partly reflect this SIP mix in a weak fresh-flow market.

Management said competition from platforms, banks and national distributors is rising, but it is holding market share; it said some large players are moderating payouts after 2-3 years of higher payouts.
Management said MF PMS fee cap of 1% is close to current ~80-90 bps realisation on MF, so margin should be similar.
Commissions as a share of non-insurance operating revenue rose to 62.6% from 61.4% in Q1, which management attributed mainly to a INR2.5 crore additional trail provision (INR1.75 crore booked in Q2).

qa_highlights.question: How would a level playing field between IDEs and IDAs change the economics, and where are insurance margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said insurance margins are broadly in line with mutual funds; it will size the opportunity once the final regulation is out, but IDEs need at least parity with IDAs to remain viable.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 12% insurance profit contribution at risk, and will POSPs survive?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the entire 12% will not disappear overnight; renewal books may persist, and the impact will be gradual. It gave no firm guidance on the eventual impact.

qa_highlights.question: Will competition for distributors pressure MF payouts?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said new entrants with higher payouts cannot sustain them long-term and that payouts are moderating; it does not see a margin challenge from new entrants.

qa_highlights.question: Why did MF yield rise slightly this quarter?

qa_highlights.answer: PCB phase 1 is INR400 crore (INR250 crore in FY27, INR100 crore in FY28). Organic capex is INR100-150 crore a year. Commissioning is expected towards the end of FY27 or the start of FY28, with incentives claimed in part and typically lagging by a year.

543573|2026-09.headline: Syrma SGS Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 73% YoY to about INR2,000 crores; FY27 growth guidance raised to 40-45%, implying about INR7,000 crores.

Operating cash flow turned positive in Q2 at about INR120 crores, and net working capital fell to 63 days from 71 days in Q1. 543591|2026-03.headline: FY26 revenue fell to INR 660.6 crore from INR 1,291.9 crore and Q4 Gross Profit turned negative at INR -6.1 crore as domestic lounge model reset.
543591|2026-03.overview: FY26 was a transition year: domestic lounge volumes fell after banks shifted from unlimited to spend-based lounge access, cutting consolidated revenue roughly in half. Adjusted EBITDA fell to INR 25.0 crore from INR 102.1 crore and PAT to INR 11.6 crore from INR 65.1 crore. Q4 FY26 was loss-making at the gross profit, EBITDA and PAT level. Management pointed to global lounges (transaction volumes up 140% YoY), the Ten11 Hospitality railway lounge acquisition, the ongoing ETT acquisition and B2C membership (DreamFolks Club 2.0) as the growth drivers. Management said FY27 would be a transition year with breakeven possibly about a year later.

Management reiterated an INR 500 crore revenue target over 5 years and said at least 50 lounges are needed to reach that scale.

segments.commentary: New lifestyle services include spa, social clubs, room upgrades, app-based airport transfers, star-hotel meals and mall coffee. DreamFolks Club 2.0 B2C membership launched about 5-6 months ago, with spend kept deliberately modest.

Cash rose to INR193.3 crore on collections, and net worth stood at INR300.4 crore. Management guided to adjusted EBITDA breakeven by next year, while holding the earlier H2 FY28 commitment.

543596|2026-06.headline: TMB Q1 FY27 net profit rose 34.97% YoY to a record INR412 crores, with total business up 23% to INR1,21,715 crores.
543596|2026-06.overview: Tamilnad Mercantile Bank reported its strongest quarter on record: net profit of INR412 crores (up 34.97% YoY), NII up 32.01%, and operating profit of INR611 crores (up 48.22%). Total business grew 23%, driven by advances up 27.01% (gold-heavy, with agri at 40% of the book) and deposits up 19.71%, with term deposits up 20.73% and CASA down 2.95% QoQ as the bank prioritised resource mobilisation. Management raised FY27 guidance for deposits, advances and total business by 2 percentage points each, and cut its cost-to-income guidance, while stating that ECL transition provisioning (INR276 crores set aside so far) will be phased in. Asset quality improved on a YoY basis, with GNPA at 0.69% and NNPA at 0.17%.

segments.commentary: 28% of advances; YoY growth of 20.09% (earlier cited 14.89%), adding about INR500 crores per quarter. Yield fell to about 10% from 10.5% as the bank widened its customer base with finer pricing.

segments.name: Retail
segments.commentary: 25% of advances. Home loans are declining but the decline is arrested; vehicle loans grew 25.7%. Retail shows a QoQ decline, which management partly attributes to migration from retail to agri gold loans.

segments.name: Others
segments.commentary: 5.62% of advances; grew 6.69% YoY. Unsecured exposure is 10 bps of the book, with NPA of about INR56 lakh.

qa_highlights.answer: CGTMSE is one route, used as a hybrid with collateral as skin in the game, not the main strategy. Management had earlier guided 46-47% cost-to-income, now revised down by about 2 percentage points; the sub-40% Q1 print included one-offs.

543596|2026-09.headline: TMB posted record Q2 FY27 net profit of INR451 crore (+42.09% YoY) on 27.25% business growth, with net NPA at 0.14%.
543596|2026-09.overview: Management reported Q2 FY27 as its eighth straight quarter of beating the prior quarter's growth, with total business up 27.25% YoY to INR1,30,237 crore and net profit at a record INR451 crore. Net interest income rose to INR807 crore and NIM was 4.19%, down about 10 bps QoQ as term-deposit mix and refinance (about INR1,000 crore at 7-7.5%) pushed up funding costs. The bank made full provisions for SMA-1 and SMA-2 ahead of ECL norms effective 1 April 2027, with provisions of INR304.24 crore against an estimated INR385 crore ECL requirement. Management raised FY27 floors for deposits (20%+) and advances (22%+), and guided NIM at 4.10% plus or minus 5 bps for the rest of the year.

segments.name: Gold loans
segments.commentary: Gold loan book about INR29,280 crore, of which agri about INR22,000 crore and retail about INR6,084 crore. Portfolio LTV 62.35%; about 3.1% of book would be above market value on a 20% gold price fall; gold loan SMA-0-to-3 at risk about INR28 crore (0.10%).

segments.name: Advances and MSME
segments.commentary: Advances up 29.32% to INR60,691 crore; MSME growth 23.62%. Unsecured exposure about 20 bps; the uptick was a loan to Kerala State Electricity Board secured against cash flows. About 52% of advances are repo-linked, 43% MCLR-linked, about 5% treasury-linked.

segments.name: Deposits
segments.commentary: Deposits up 25.49% to INR69,546 crore, with term deposits up about 29%. Non-callable deposits were 40.62% of incremental term deposits (INR7,570 crore in H1). FCNR(B) raised about USD51.94 million; 1-year FCNR(B) rate now about 4.25%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 deposit growth floor raised to 20%+ from earlier 18%+; advances growth floor 22%+; CASA growth about 17% in H2.
NIM guided at 4.10% plus or minus 5 bps for the rest of FY27, versus the earlier 4% guidance.
Cost to income expected to rise from 38.28% but stay well below 44% as branches open and IT investment continues.
Target of 60 branch openings in FY27 (9 opened in H1), with 20+ outside Tamil Nadu by year-end.
Long-term aim is to grow 4-5 percentage points faster than the industry over the next 3-5 years.
CD ratio can rise to 98% against 87.27% currently, given net worth of 12.53% of the balance sheet.
capex_capacity: Nine branches opened in H1 FY27; 60 planned for the year, with 37 opened YoY (15 outside Tamil Nadu).
Business per employee at INR25 crore; profit per employee about INR35 lakh.
Ongoing IT investment and data/process automation cited as drivers of productivity and cost pressure.
Leverage ratio 11.99% vs 3.50% requirement; LCR 139.43%; NSFR 146.15%.
demand_pricing: Investment portfolio rose to about 22% of the balance sheet, yielding about 7% vs about 10.3% on advances, which weighed on margin mix.
Repo cut passthrough is automatic at each loan's quarterly reset; the 25 bps repo move flows to the 5.5% benchmark over about three months.
Refinance of about INR1,000 crore taken from SIDBI at 7-7.5% during the quarter.
Bulk deposits are 19% of total deposits; the bulk share of the INR7,570 crore incremental term deposits was not disclosed on the call.
Management sees no material oil-price impact so far on export credit or MSME books; drought risk is being monitored through daily gold LTV tracking.

qa_highlights.question: What is the split of gold loans between agri and retail, and how much of the book is repo-linked?
qa_highlights.answer: Gold loans total INR29,280 crore: agri about INR22,000 crore and retail INR6,084 crore. About 52% of advances are repo-linked (reset quarterly), 43% MCLR-linked, about 5% treasury-linked.

qa_highlights.question: Will the bank sustain high growth and how is the oil price affecting it?
qa_highlights.answer: The target is to grow 4-5 percentage points above industry growth over 3-5 years, not a fixed 20-30% rate. No oil-price impact seen yet in export credit or MSME.

qa_highlights.question: How has NIM and yield on advances moved, and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Yield on advances rose to 10.32% from 10.10% as advances were repriced to offset higher deposit costs. NIM guided at 4.10% plus or minus 5 bps for the rest of FY27, with management calling it a floor.

qa_highlights.question: Will the cost to income ratio rise, and what is the guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Cost to income is expected to move up from 38.28% due to branch openings and IT spend, but to stay well below 44%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of the IRDAI insurance norms?
qa_highlights.answer: Insurance commission is only about INR9 crore in H1. Management estimated about a 20% reduction in that income, which incremental business would offset.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the disputed share ownership matter, and would it block a bonus or split?
qa_highlights.answer: The Appellate Tribunal order dated 9 July has not been appealed by the bank or ED within the window. The bank has applied to RBI to regularise the share transfer, and management said this does not block a bonus or split.

543597|2026-03.headline: FY26 revenue rose about 18% to INR823 crore and EBITDA reached about INR86 crore (10.4% margin), with Q4 revenue at about INR317 crore.
543597|2026-03.overview: Management described FY26 as a recovery year after a difficult H1, with consolidated revenue of about INR823 crore (up about 18%), EBITDA up from about INR60 crore to about INR86 crore, and margin up from 8.6% to 10.4%. 543599|2026-06.headline: Ksolves Q1 FY27 revenue rose 10% YoY to Rs 41.4 crore, but management withdrew FY27 revenue guidance while EBITDA margin hit 30.3%.
543599|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue for Q1 FY27 (quarter ended 30 June 2026) was Rs 41.4 crore, up 10% YoY but down 3.7% QoQ, as two long-standing large clients cut work and some engagement ramp-downs landed late in the quarter. EBITDA was Rs 12.56 crore (up 26.2% YoY, flat QoQ) with margin at 30.3%, and PAT was Rs 9.21 crore (up 43.3% YoY, down 5% QoQ). Management said it would not reaffirm FY27 revenue guidance, now expecting flat-to-4-5% growth at most, and reiterated a 25-30% EBITDA margin range. The company remains debt-free and declared an interim dividend of Rs 4 per share.

543599|2026-09.headline: Ksolves Q2 FY27 revenue fell 4.7% YoY to INR 37.8 crores on client ramp-downs; EBITDA margin 25.7%, within guided band.
543599|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue was INR 37.8 crores, down 4.7% YoY and 8.8% QoQ, driven by client-specific ramp-downs at a couple of large enterprise accounts and cautious client spending. EBITDA was INR 9.7 crores at a 25.7% margin (vs 30.3% in Q1 and 30.4% in Q2 FY26), which management attributed to lower revenue partly offset by cost actions and AI-led productivity. PAT was INR 7.25 crores (19.2% margin), and H1 revenue grew 2.5% YoY to INR 79.2 crores. Management guided FY27 revenue to trail FY26 and EBITDA margin to stay within 25-30%, with H2 focus on pipeline building, AI opportunities and enterprise account recovery.

financial_highlights.change: vs 30.3% in Q1 FY27 and 30.4% in Q2 FY26
broadly in line with H1 FY26

financial_highlights.value: INR 1 per share second interim; H1 total INR 5 per share (~72% of H1 PAT)

segments.name: IT services
segments.commentary: Core business at 98.4% of Q2 revenue. Geography: North America 59%, India 20%, Europe 6%, Australia 4%, rest of world 11%; overseas 80%.

segments.name: BFSI / banking
segments.commentary: Three Q2 wins in banking (South America, UK, Europe). BFSI share of revenue rose from 7% to 8% (H1 FY26 vs H1 FY27 per analyst slide); management says the jump comes from H2. Company has about 11-12 BFSI clients.

segments.name: Telecom
segments.commentary: Largest segment at about 25% of revenue this year vs 27% last year per analyst reading of slides; one telecom client that was closing its business is now re-engaging.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue expected to remain soft and trail FY26 levels; company did not reaffirm earlier guidance.

Full-quarter benefit of Q2 cost actions expected from end of Q3.

Dividend to be decided each year based on profitability and cash needs; shareholder returns remain a priority.
capex_capacity: Headcount fell about 10% from ~550 to ~495; hiring in FY27 limited to 5-10% of last year's level, and capacity is to be filled from the existing team before new hiring.
AI productivity: management says one person can now deliver 2x-3x prior output.

Built a low-code/no-code agent platform for a telecom client used by 500+ operations staff; migrated a US client's legacy codebase with 8 agents in about 7-8 months versus an estimated 1-1.5 years manually.
Opened a sales office in Australia for local bids; delivery team is based in India.
Being a Select Partner in Anthropic (Claude) and OpenAI networks; 100% of engineers Claude certified.
demand_pricing: Client spending remains selective and discretionary spend under scrutiny; management said clients had put decisions on hold until around 10 September over AI wait-and-watch, and are now returning with AI-led requirements.
Customers now ask for Odoo, Salesforce or data engineering with agentic AI; management says the sales question has shifted from headcount to business outcome.
Two large enterprise accounts ramped down; management called these client-specific, not structural, and said the pipeline was not deep enough to offset them in the quarter.
Management said some clients tested building in-house AI tools but have since returned to outsourcing projects for features.
Top 10 clients contributed 50% of revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Will dividends continue at around 100% of PAT?
qa_highlights.answer: Shareholder returns remain a priority; the Board will decide each payout based on yearly profitability and cash needs. H1 interim dividend totalled INR 5 per share (~72% of H1 PAT).

qa_highlights.question: Do you have constant-currency numbers given rupee weakness?
qa_highlights.answer: No, the company is not currently calculating revenue in constant currency.

qa_highlights.question: How much revenue was lost from the two clients?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give a number, but said it was large enough to be a big hit; new Q1 and Q2 wins absorbed much of it, though a deficit remained.

qa_highlights.question: How will the margin move with sales traction?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins would be at the upper end of the guided range if revenue recovers; the INR 3.6 crore revenue drop was the main driver of the Q2 margin dip.

qa_highlights.question: Will the banking wins contribute meaningfully, and how big can BFSI become?
qa_highlights.answer: Projects are underway and take months to quarters; the South American bank relationship is ongoing but expansion is not in writing. Management hopes other banks will follow.

qa_highlights.question: Are you entering cybersecurity?
qa_highlights.answer: Still exploring; management sees AI guardrails and security as a demand opportunity but has not defined the offering.

Client concentration: top 10 clients are 50% of revenue, and two large accounts ramped down in Q2.
Currency: management does not track constant-currency revenue despite a weaker rupee, so FX effect on reported numbers is not visible.
Management did not reaffirm prior guidance; new cybersecurity vertical is still undefined.

rows.why: Management is optimistic about FY28 growth with a 20%-plus aspiration, but this is conditional on geopolitical stability and the H2 recovery, and was not quantified.

543600|2026-03.headline: Harsha Engineers Q4 FY26 Engineering EBITDA rose to INR77 crore; FY26 Engineering revenue INR1,444 crore, guided to double-digit FY27 growth.
543600|2026-03.overview: Management reported Q4 FY26 consolidated Engineering revenue of INR382 crore and EBITDA of INR77 crore, versus adjusted EBITDA of INR64.3 crore in Q3 and INR66 crore in Q4 FY25. For FY26, Engineering revenue grew to INR1,444 crore from INR1,269 crore, with consolidated EBITDA of INR264 crore (about INR270 crore adjusted for the new Labour Code impact). Solar revenue was INR183 crore with PAT of INR10.2 crore. Management guided to double-digit FY27 consolidated growth, with India Engineering in the mid-teens, and to maintaining current margins. The call also covered weak Romania profitability, the Advantek ramp-up, and the China steel-cage expansion.

financial_highlights.change: Engineering revenue growth of about 15.7% YoY excluding Solar; consolidated growth of about 27% including Solar
vs adjusted INR64.3 crore in Q3 FY26 and INR66 crore in Q4 FY25

financial_highlights.value: INR264 crore reported; about INR270 crore adjusted for Labour Code impact

financial_highlights.change: PAT INR10.2 crore vs adjusted PAT INR5 crore in FY25

financial_highlights.value: Positive EBITDA INR4 crore; combined loss INR11.4 crore (management also cited INR11.5 crore)
Turnover about INR120 crore; PAT about INR5 crore profit; EBITDA about 11%
Turnover about INR247 crore; PAT loss about INR14 crore

financial_highlights.metric: FY26 combined loss of foreign subsidiaries
financial_highlights.value: INR9 crore (management correction from INR11 crore); prior year INR14 crore

financial_highlights.change: vs 134 days in previous quarter and 127 days in previous year

financial_highlights.value: INR120 crore consolidated; about INR20 crore in Q4

segments.name: Bearing cages (India Engineering)
segments.commentary: India-to-India cage business grew about 11% in FY26 per management. Large-size cages grew about 14% to about INR49 crore, with mid-teens to 15-20% growth expected.

segments.name: Bushings
segments.commentary: Revenue INR127 crore in FY26, up about 25%, driven by design conversion in wind planetary gearboxes from bearings to bushings. Management targets 25-30% growth in FY27.

segments.name: Stampings
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue about INR60 crore. Growth drivers are AC compressor components and white goods. Management expects at least 20% growth next year and 15-20% mid-term.

segments.name: Solar
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR183 crore with PAT INR10.2 crore. Q4 revenue about INR91 crore, roughly doubled YoY. Management expects more than 25% growth and Solar EBITDA margin to hold near the FY26 level.

segments.name: Advantek (India, subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Still at low utilisation; FY26 EBITDA INR4 crore but net loss about INR11 crore on depreciation and interest. Sales expected to grow at least 3x in FY27; current installed capacity seen generating INR250-300 crore turnover.

segments.name: China subsidiary
segments.commentary: FY26 turnover about INR120 crore, PAT about INR5 crore profit. Brownfield steel-cage expansion to be commissioned in H2 FY28; INR70 crore capex in FY27 and INR20 crore in FY28.

segments.name: Romania subsidiary
segments.commentary: FY26 turnover about INR247 crore with PAT loss about INR14 crore. Cage share of mix at about 22%, targeted to rise to 30-35%. Wind market in Europe not yet recovered.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated revenue growth expected to be double-digit, with India Engineering in the mid-teens; India growth described as high-teens to mid-teens in the Q&A.
Management expects to at least maintain current margin profile in FY27, with an aim to improve it.
Over 2-3 years, management expects consolidated EBITDA to rise 100-200 basis points; India Engineering EBITDA has been consistently about 20%.
Maintenance capex in India of INR30-40 crore in FY27 and a similar amount in FY28; China expansion capex of about INR70 crore in FY27 and INR20 crore in FY28.
Advantek subsidiary expected to reach peak with current installed capacity in about two years; a second-phase capex plan is to be finalised in the next few weeks, with work starting this year.
Management indicated the India-level business could reach INR2,400-2,500 crore and consolidated INR2,700-3,000 crore on current capabilities, depending on capacity additions.
capex_capacity: Harsha has three facilities in India (the third, at Bhayla, commissioned in FY26), one in Romania and one in China.

Advantek is in its first year of operations and running at low utilisation; its sales are expected to grow at least 3x in FY27. Second-phase Advantek capex is being firmed up for additional capacity in key growth verticals.
China brownfield steel-cage expansion has begun; it will add steel cages to a predominantly brass-based portfolio, with commissioning in H2 FY28.
Management said the Advantek capex includes infrastructure that will not translate immediately into fixed-asset-to-revenue multiples.
Saket Kapoor noted PP&E closing balance of about INR615 crore.
demand_pricing: Export growth of about 17% in FY26 was attributed to improving European and US industrial markets; US import tariff on cages was cut to zero, aiding US picks-up.

Pass-through of raw-material costs (steel, brass, metal prices) to customers is contractual, with an average lag of about four months. Q4 growth was mainly volume-driven, as metal prices moved mainly from late December to February/March.

Europe demand is improving slowly, but management said there is no definitive recovery and that cost and pricing issues remain. Europe is about 30% of sales, China just over 10%, US 6-7% and Japan about 2%.
Domestic bearing makers are ramping capacity and are expected to invest further; management is bullish, though it flagged risks from the war and petroleum prices.
Cost pressure is building from oils, lubricants and plastic cage material; logistics has not been impacted so far. Management is working to mitigate or pass through these costs.
Management said wallet share is about 70-90% in India but only 10-20% with large overseas customers and 2-3% with the Japan-based customer.

qa_highlights.question: How much of Q4 revenue growth came from pricing versus volume, and was commodity inflation fully passed through?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 27% consolidated growth was mainly Solar; Engineering grew 15.7% YoY. Growth was mostly volume-led, and pass-through is automatic with an average lag of about four months.

qa_highlights.question: What were the absolute FY26 revenue and PBT figures for the China and Romania subsidiaries?
qa_highlights.answer: China: turnover about INR120 crore with PAT about INR5 crore profit. Romania: turnover about INR247 crore with PAT loss about INR14 crore. Combined subsidiary loss was INR9 crore after correction; management said losses would reduce significantly.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for Europe demand and restructuring?
qa_highlights.answer: Europe is slowly improving, with no sharp recovery. Restructuring is ongoing, the cost structure is not yet right, and Romania still has negative margins. Management is evaluating how long it can sustain these margins.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex plan for FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: India maintenance capex of INR30-40 crore per year; China expansion INR70 crore in FY27 and INR20 crore in FY28; further Advantek phase-two capex is being finalised.

qa_highlights.question: What is Advantek's ramp-up timeline and revenue potential?
qa_highlights.answer: Current installed capacity expected to peak in about two years, with turnover of INR250-300 crore. Expansion beyond that is planned.

qa_highlights.question: What drives bushing growth and what is the stamping outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Bushing growth comes from design conversion in wind planetary gearboxes away from bearings. Stampings (about INR60 crore in FY26) are driven by AC compressor and white goods components; management expects at least 20% growth next year.

Advantek: low utilisation, FY26 net loss about INR11 crore on depreciation and interest; second-phase capex plan to be finalised in the next few weeks and its size not yet disclosed.

Geographic mix and Solar growth (about 100% in Q4) drove the headline 27% growth; track Engineering-only growth (15.7%) against the mid-teens FY27 guidance.

key_quotes: And on your questions for the pass -through mechanism, yes, it is very well-established pass-through mechanism with the customer.
So, we are very bullish. There could be impact of, you know, current war and petroleum prices and all that.
So, last whole year, we are seeing demand has slowly improved over the year.
We are continuing to face massive inflationary pressure in Europe, which is also adding to this whole challenge.

543600|2026-06.headline: Harsha Engineers Q1 FY27 consolidated Engineering supply up 25% YoY to Rs 421 crore, but EBITDA margin compressed on a 6-7% raw material spike pending pass-through.

Management kept FY27 guidance of high-teens India growth and low-teens consolidated growth, with India Engineering EBITDA margin of 22-24%.

rows.why: Guidance was held (40% to 50% revenue CAGR, 20% to 25% EBITDA margin) and management called it realistic, not conservative, so there is no sign of a raise.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Working capital and short-term debt rose sharply with no peak debt or cash-flow-positive timeline given, Fusion Electronics has no meaningful revenue yet, and the 4,500-unit Kavach tender (closed 14 April 2026) has no outcome, so execution and cash risks are open.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Kavach trial completion and ISA approval are targeted within FY27 (geopolitical factors cited as a constraint), and the green mobility retrofit was already demonstrated, but no dated product launch was given.

rows.label: Kavach 4,500-unit loco tender outcome pending
rows.why: The tender for about 4,500 loco units closed 14 April 2026 with no outcome yet, and management said finalisation takes time and Concord has quoted several tenders, so a win would be large but timing is open.

rows.label: Fusion Electronics first revenue year
rows.why: Management expects revenue contribution this year with about INR 200 crore full-scale potential, but gave no figure and cited a typical 300-day integration cycle, with no meaningful revenue so far.

rows.label: Working capital and debt peak
rows.why: Management said Q1 receivables will be high and working capital will spike with the INR 697 crore order book before easing, with no peak debt estimate or positive operating cash flow timeline given.

tone.note: Management was confident on the long-term railway platform, order book and sovereign-backed payments, but cautious and evasive on Fusion revenue, Kavach tender timing, loco count, peak debt and cash-flow timing; analysts pressed on receivables, short-term debt, margin conservatism and liquidity.

543620|2026-03.headline: FY26 revenue rose 61% to INR2,146 crore and PAT 59% to INR201 crore; cell line guided to lift EBITDA margin toward 20%+ later.
543620|2026-03.overview: Insolation Energy listed on BSE and NSE Main Board on 9 March 2026. FY26 revenue from operations was INR2,146 crore (up 61%), EBITDA INR305 crore (up 79%, margin 14% vs 13%), and PAT INR201 crore (up 59%). Q4 FY26 revenue was INR794 crore (up 100% YoY), with EBITDA INR111 crore and PAT INR70 crore, though management said utility-scale dispatches cluster in the last month of each quarter. Management is building a 4.5 GW TOPCon cell line and 4.5 GW aluminium frame plant at Narmadapuram, with cell COD targeted for Q3/Q4 FY27 and frames in Q1 FY27.

financial_highlights.metric: Net debt to equity / ROCE / ROE

financial_highlights.value: INR835 crore (long-term INR468 crore; short-term INR300 crore)
financial_highlights.change: from INR108 crore a year earlier

segments.name: Solar modules
segments.commentary: FY26 sales mix was about 85% non-DCR and 15% DCR. Module capacity is 5.5 GW. Management targets about 2 GW production and sales from modules in FY27, with non-DCR at 2-2.5 GW and DCR cells sourced externally on top.

segments.name: EPC
segments.commentary: Very nascent; minimal revenue in Q4 FY26. A third-party order of over INR300 crore secured last year is expected to contribute revenue in FY27.

segments.name: IPP (KUSUM)
segments.commentary: Targeting about 325 MW AC / 400 MW DC, with 38-40 MW commissioned so far. FY27 IPP revenue guided at about INR135 crore; FY28 at about INR300 crore. Capex about INR1,000 crore.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at least equal to FY26 (about 50-60%), subject to market conditions; FY28 revenue target above INR5,000 crore.
EBITDA margin in FY27 expected at 14-15% including aluminium frame integration; management says 20%+ once the full cell line runs (FY28 framing).
FY27 capex about INR2,500 crore: about INR1,500 crore for the cell line (including working capital margin and contingency) and about INR1,000 crore for KUSUM IPP.
Positive free cash flow expected 6-8 months after cell plant goes live (Q4 FY27), per CFO.
Wafer/ingot plant (4.5 GW, CZ technology, about INR1,000-1,200 crore capex) to be funded mainly from internal accruals; DPR due in 2-3 months.
Peak debt expected near INR1,500 crore in FY27; IREDA loan of INR1,134 crore, 12-month moratorium then 7-year repayment, at 8.95% post-COD.
capex_capacity: Sawarda Unit 3 (INR320 crore) fully operational with all three lines running.

4.5 GW TOPCon cell line at Narmadapuram: INR340 crore drawn from IREDA by 31 March 2026; expected to start ramp-up in Q4 FY27, full ramp about 3-4 months later (management said full utilisation by Q1 FY28).
Aluminium frame plant (4.5 GW) expected to commission in Q1 FY27; mainly for internal use.
Next phase: 4.5 GW ingot and wafer on 70,000 sq m of land acquired in Narmadapuram; about 20 acres remain. ALMM Part 3 effective 1 June 2028 is the stated timing driver.
Cell line plant efficiency target above 80%; management says the cell capacity is used internally first, with any surplus sold in the open market.
demand_pricing: Current order book of about 1.6-1.8 GW for this year, per management; about 50% of FY27 capacity already booked, with the rest refilled monthly from distributors, OEM white-label and KUSUM partners.
Non-DCR module prices about INR13-14/W; DCR about INR20-22/W (Mono PERC INR20-21, TOPCon INR21-22, up to INR22.5 in some locations).
Sales mix by segment in FY26: utility about 65%, KUSUM about 15%, PM Surya Ghar about 5%, OEM about 5%, miscellaneous about 10%.

Raw-material cost pressure noted; management said it will pass through some increase and absorb some, relying on about 2-3 months of raw material held in inventory against orders. Escalation clauses are mostly USD-linked.
Management estimates about 30 GW of non-ALMM modules in the market, and said non-DCR cell demand remains for 1-1.5 years of tenders.

qa_highlights.question: Is there visibility on FY27 volume and margin after the cell line comes on?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided about 2 GW module production and sales in FY27 and 14-15% EBITDA margin, rising to 20%+ with the full cell line. Ravi said margins could be revised upward if market conditions allow.

qa_highlights.question: Why did December and March not sustain the run rate of Q4 revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said utility-scale dispatches are concentrated in the last month of each quarter, with about INR350 crore in December and about INR440 crore in March, and that this is an industry pattern.

qa_highlights.question: What is the working capital and debt picture after receivables rose 156%?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said short-term borrowing rose because of capacity scale-up, and that orders are now on 45-day LCs, which lifts receivables. IREDA drawdown of INR340 crore is largely parked in FDs of about INR300 crore; the remaining drawdowns are expected within 2-3 months.

qa_highlights.question: What is the interest cost on borrowings?
qa_highlights.answer: IREDA loan sanctioned at 9.20% pre-COD and 8.95% post-COD. Working capital borrowings are close to 8%.

risks_watch: Raw-material cost inflation and the ability to pass it through, given that price escalation is mainly USD-linked and orders are priced ahead.
Cell line ramp timing (Q4 FY27 start, full utilisation by Q1 FY28); next two quarters' utilisation guided at only 60-70%.
Heavy reliance on Chinese equipment for the cell line; management cites a two-year on-site support contract with the supplier.
Quarter-end-loaded dispatches make quarterly revenue and receivables lumpy; receivables rose to INR280 crore.
Negative FCFF (CFO's FCF yield cited as -15.9%) until the cell plant is operating; peak debt near INR1,500 crore in FY27.
Wafer/ingot plant (INR1,000-1,200 crore) remains at DPR stage with no technology partner named; the CZ technology choice is still under consideration.
543620|2026-03.management_tone: Confident and expansive on long-term growth and margins, but hedged on near-term figures, repeatedly tying guidance to market conditions. Answers were sometimes inconsistent (for example, on the FY27 margin and capex funding), and several questions had to be re-asked.
key_quotes: we definitely we assure that whatever the growth in FY 26 should be there, the revenue growth in FY27 at least should be there.
Yes, definitely, our EBITDA margin should increase when our cell is operational.
Usually the solar cell efficiencies are much higher than the modules. We are targeting for more than 80% of the plant efficiency.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management targets about 2 GW module production and sales in FY27 versus the FY26 base, with FY27 revenue growth guided at least 50-60%, backed by a 1.6-1.8 GW order book and about 50% of FY27 capacity already booked.

rows.why: FY27 capex guided at about INR2,500 crore (INR1,500 crore cell line, INR1,000 crore KUSUM IPP), and a 4.5 GW ingot/wafer plant (INR1,000-1,200 crore) has a DPR due in 2-3 months with 20 acres of land still remaining at Narmadapuram.

rows.when: Q1 FY27 (aluminium frames); Q3/Q4 FY27 (TOPCon cells)
rows.why: The 4.5 GW aluminium frame plant is due in Q1 FY27 mainly for internal use, and the 4.5 GW TOPCon cell line targets COD in Q3/Q4 FY27 with cell efficiency target above 80%.

rows.when: FY27 peak; positive FCF 6-8 months after cell plant goes liv
rows.why: Total borrowings rose to INR835 crore from INR108 crore a year earlier, peak debt is guided near INR1,500 crore in FY27, and the CFO expects positive free cash flow 6-8 months after cell plant COD, though FCFF yield is cited at -15.9% until then.

rows.label: FY28 revenue above INR5,000 crore
rows.why: Management targets FY28 revenue above INR5,000 crore versus FY26 INR2,146 crore, which depends on the cell line ramp and market conditions, with IPP revenue guided at about INR300 crore in FY28.

rows.label: Receivables and quarter-end loading
rows.why: Trade receivables rose 156% YoY to INR280 crore as orders moved to 45-day LCs and dispatches cluster in the last month of each quarter (about INR350 crore in December and INR440 crore in March).

tone.note: Management was confident on long-term growth, the frame plant and the cell line, and on margins of 20%+ in FY28, but hedged near-term figures against market conditions; analysts and the brief flagged inconsistency on FY27 margin and capex funding, and several questions were re-asked.

543626|2026-03.headline: Electronics Mart Q4 FY26 revenue rose 15% to INR1,913 crores and SSSG hit 12.2%, with EBITDA margin up to 6.7%.
543626|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue grew 15% YoY to INR1,913 crores, with EBITDA up 20% to INR129 crores and margin expanding to 6.7% from 5.6%. Same-store sales growth was 12.2% in the quarter, helped by GST rate cuts, festive demand and mobile launches, while FY26 SSSG was 5.3%. FY26 revenue rose 7% to INR7,183 crores with EBITDA of INR438 crores (6.1% margin) and PAT of INR107 crores. Management said working capital requirements have fallen and pre Ind AS operating cash flow reached INR299 crores for the year.

segments.name: South cluster (AP, Telangana, Hyderabad)
segments.commentary: Management cites a 6.5% EBITDA margin for the South cluster, with about INR6,000-6,500 crores of revenue from the region (69 AP stores, 46 Telangana, 72 Hyderabad city). Hyderabad city generated about INR4,122 crores in FY26; Hyderabad SSSG was double-digit in Q4.

segments.name: North cluster (NCR/Delhi)
segments.commentary: Delhi NCR operates 35 stores with about INR590 crores of revenue in FY26 and is now EBITDA positive on a full-year basis. Management guided to 25-30% growth in FY27 and a 2.5-3% EBITDA margin, versus about 0.2-0.3% now; Q4 Delhi like-to-like sales were reported at about 19%.

segments.name: Mature vs new stores
segments.commentary: Of 223 stores, 83 are over 4 years old (about 7.3% EBITDA margin) and 140 are under 4 years old (about 3.1% margin).

segments.name: Product categories
segments.commentary: Panels grew 13% and mobile phones 28% in Q4; washing machines grew strongly in double digits, refrigerators were stable, and large appliance mix fell from 47% to 42%.

guidance_outlook: Organic store additions of about 20 in FY27 (12-15 in NCR and AP/Telangana per management, plus Delhi and South openings), with capex of about INR3-4 crores per store assumed for 8,000-10,000 sq ft stores.
New East entry starting with 5-7 stores in Kolkata by end-Q2 or start-Q3 FY27; FY27 real estate spend of about INR50 crores, up to INR100 crores over 12-14 months.

NCR revenue target of INR800+ crores in FY27 (vs INR585 crores in FY26), with 2-4% EBITDA margin; Andhra Pradesh (INR1,100+ crores) and Telangana (INR1,000 crores) expected to deliver higher single-digit SSSG.
North cluster margin to be 3-4% higher than now by FY28 (not stated as an exact level).
Management expects ASPs up at least 5-6% on average in FY26 with volume held; price hikes are passed through to customers; inventory to be bought 2-3% higher at newer prices for the next 20 days.
capex_capacity: Store count 223 (83 over 4 years old, 140 under 4 years); Q4 added 4 stores (NCR, Telangana, 2 in Andhra Pradesh).
Management plans 12-15 organic stores in NCR, AP and Telangana, with 4-5 Delhi stores getting ready, and 7-8 more stores in NCR; new Kolkata cluster to start with 5-7 stores by end-Q2 or start-Q3.
Store size 8,000-10,000 sq ft typical, capex about INR3-4 crores per store, similar product mix in new regions.
Working capital requirement reduced; cash flow prioritised over expansion, with loans against property repaid organically.
Franchise model not in use; all stores company-operated, with franchising only to be explored if OEMs support it.
demand_pricing: Q4 demand robust across categories; washing machines grew strongly in double digits, panels 13%, mobile phones 28% (new launches in January and March).
ASPs rose at least 5-6% on average in FY26 for the same volume (bigger TV sizes after GST cut, higher-star ACs), and management says no category saw ASP decline.
Price hikes on RAC products of about INR1,500-2,000 per SKU are passed on to customers; additional inventory bought at 2-3% higher prices.
Entry-level mobile price hikes (below INR20,000) have limited impact, as the company's mobile ASP is about INR35,000-40,000.
Sourcing is essentially direct from OEMs/brands; distributor purchases are about INR50 crores a year, with margins unchanged.
Competition: NCR faces Croma, Reliance and Vijay Sales; South competes mostly with mom-and-pop stores, which drives the margin gap.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Hyderabad SSSG double-digit in Q4 and how should FY27 be read?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to the GST cut benefit across categories (TVs, washing machines, dishwashers, refrigerators, cooling products) plus mobile launches; early Q1 trends were good.

qa_highlights.question: How did gross margin hold up as large appliance mix fell from 47% to 42%?
qa_highlights.answer: Margins were supported by higher-margin categories (mobile accessories, built-in appliances, audio) and better throughput; management expects margins to hold or improve.

qa_highlights.question: Store opening cadence and cash flow deployment?
qa_highlights.answer: Store openings slowed as Delhi was a new market in FY25; Hyderabad adds only 1-2 stores a year. Management said cash is reinvested, working capital has fallen and loans are repaid organically.

qa_highlights.question: Delhi/NCR margin path?
qa_highlights.answer: Targets INR800+ crores revenue and 2-4% EBITDA margin in FY27, with a 3-4% higher margin than now by FY28; the NCR cluster is EBITDA positive for the full year.

qa_highlights.question: Franchise model?
qa_highlights.answer: No franchising currently; management said it would consider franchising only in a region where OEM support and partner alignment exist, citing seasonality and consumer experience.

qa_highlights.question: Why enter Kolkata while NCR is still stabilising?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Delhi stabilisation is done and growth will be organic; Kolkata is a new cluster with a 12-14 month learning cycle, starting with 5-7 stores by end-Q2 or start-Q3.

risks_watch: Delhi/NCR execution: Q4 growth was off a low base, and management targets 25-30% growth and a 2.5-3% margin in FY27 from a 0.2-0.3% base.
Summer and cooling demand: Delhi started late, and about 50% of Q1 remained at the time of the call; cooling products are key to the quarter's margin.
Store maturity: 140 stores under 4 years old run at 3.1% margin versus 7.3% for mature stores.
Working capital and inventory: inventory days were 73 at 31 March 2026; RAC inventory was bought at older prices, with more purchases at higher prices expected.
Kolkata entry is new and capital-intensive (up to INR100 crores of real estate over 12-14 months).
543626|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on South/Hyderabad and the margin trajectory, but more measured on Delhi, where management said growth will be more organic. Some answers were evasive on volume-versus-value splits and on Q1 trends.
key_quotes: We also saw a meaningful operating leverage coming through, resulting in an improvement in our operating margins, even as we continue to add new stores to our network.
Mature stores continue to demonstrate strong performance with an EBITDA margin of approximately 7.3%, while newer stores are currently operating at 3.1%, consistent with their stage of ramp-up.
So Calcutta would be a new base for East.

rows.why: Management expects FY27 SSSG of higher single digits in AP (INR1,100+ crore) and Telangana (INR1,000 crore), NCR revenue of INR800+ crore vs INR585 crore in FY26 (+25-30%), and ~20 new stores added, though FY26 SSSG was 5.3% with ASP up 5-6% and volume held.

rows.why: Q4 SSSG was 12.2% with Hyderabad double-digit and early Q1 trends described as good, but the GST-cut and mobile-launch benefits may fade and management was evasive on Q1 trends.

rows.why: No specific new product or brand launch was guided; mobile launches in January and March drove a 28% Q4 mobile growth but were not framed as a forward pipeline.

rows.why: Pre Ind AS operating cash flow reached INR299 crore in FY26 and loans against property are being repaid organically, with inventory at 73 days on 31 March 2026.

rows.why: 5-7 stores guided in Kolkata with about INR50 crore real estate spend in FY27, rising to INR100 crore over 12-14 months.

rows.why: Price hikes of INR1,500-2,000 per SKU on RAC are passed to customers, with inventory bought 2-3% higher and FY26 ASP up at least 5-6% at unchanged volume.

543626|2026-06.headline: Electronics Mart Q1 FY27 revenue rose 39% to INR 2,419 crore and PAT to INR 121 crore, with reported EBITDA margin at 9.9%.
543626|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 was the company's strongest quarter to date, driven by a strong AC season, healthy footfalls and conversions, and 34.2% same-store sales growth. Gross margin expanded to 17.2% from 14.6%, aided by cooling-product mix and temporary price-increase gains in IT hardware. Working capital days fell to 42 from 73 and working capital borrowings dropped to INR 97 crore from INR 658 crore at the start of the quarter. Management guided FY27 revenue growth of 18-20% and a post-Ind AS EBITDA margin of 7.5-8%, and said the margin tailwinds are partly temporary.

segments.name: Large appliances
segments.commentary: 48% of revenue, led by air conditioners, with traction in washing machines and refrigerators. AC season was the best quarter yet by volume and value.

segments.name: Mobile phones
segments.commentary: 39% of revenue in Q1 FY27, down from 40% in the comparable base, as cooling-product mix rose seasonally.

segments.name: South cluster
segments.commentary: Revenue +40% YoY with EBITDA margin of 10.9%. Andhra Pradesh revenue +62% (SSG 49.1%), Telangana up-country +48% (SSG 40%), Hyderabad city +34% (SSG 32.3%).

segments.name: North cluster
segments.commentary: Revenue +29% YoY with record EBITDA margin of 4.9%. Management said North market for cooling products was negative versus 2024.

segments.name: Store maturity
segments.commentary: 96 stores older than 4 years run at 11.2% EBITDA margin; 131 stores under 4 years old delivered 8.1%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at 18-20% YoY, described as 'very easily achievable'; upside possible if Q4 season is strong. Management declined to commit to INR 10,000 crore revenue.
FY27 full-year gross margin guided at 15-15.5%, below the Q1 level, as Q1 benefited from temporary price-increase gains.
Post-Ind AS EBITDA margin guided at 7.5-8% for FY27; management called 9% 'too optimistic'.
Finance cost expected to be at least INR 10 crore lower than last year's ~INR 150 crore.
Plan to open 25-30 stores in FY27 across existing geographies and West Bengal; 5 Kolkata stores by Diwali and 10-12 by end-Q4 FY27; 8-10 NCR stores in FY27 and about 5 South stores.
West Bengal capex about INR 100 crore for stores plus about INR 50 crore for property purchases over the next two years, funded from internal accruals.
risks_watch: Gross margin tailwind from temporary price-increase gains in laptops and mobiles may reverse; management guides FY27 gross margin to 15-15.5%.
Delhi NCR same-store sales weak as North cooling-product market declined; management expects improvement but gave no quarterly figures.
Memory-chip shortages may force higher stock levels (50-60 days instead of 30) for some IT and mobile SKUs.
Management could not quantify the share of inventory bought at lower prior-year cost, so the gross margin benefit is hard to isolate.
Quality of the Q1 base: the comparison is against a weak AC season in Q1 FY26, so the growth rate may not persist.
New store ramp in West Bengal and North; execution against 25-30 openings a year and the 10-12 Kolkata target by March 2027.

vs INR 658 crore at start of quarter

qa_highlights.question: What are full-year FY27 revenue and gross margin targets, given the weak base?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue growth of 18-20% is described as very easily achievable; management declined to commit to INR 10,000 crore. FY27 gross margin guided at 15-15.5%, with Q1's 17.2% partly temporary from price-increase gains.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the gross margin expansion and is the benefit sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited higher cooling-product mix and buying laptops and mobiles at lower prices during price rises; it called the price-increase gain temporary and could not quantify the low-cost inventory share.

qa_highlights.question: Is post-Ind AS EBITDA margin at 8-9% achievable and what is the finance cost outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said 9% is too optimistic and 7.5-8% is easily achievable; finance cost to be at least INR 10 crore lower than last year's ~INR 150 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Delhi NCR SSG weak and what store openings are planned there and in Kolkata?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the North cooling market declined versus 2024 and the base was small; Kolkata has 5 stores by Diwali and 10-12 by March 2027; NCR 8-10 stores this year.

qa_highlights.question: Capex requirement for West Bengal and funding?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR 100 crore for stores plus about INR 50 crore for property purchases over two years, all funded from internal accruals; about 30 stores in Kolkata over 24 months.

qa_highlights.question: Can the company quantify its market share gains and volume versus price contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Market share gains estimated at 4% to 12% outside Hyderabad depending on the geography; growth attributed mainly to volume, with ASP up only in limited categories.

capex_capacity: Plans 25-30 store openings in FY27 across existing geographies and West Bengal; 5 Kolkata stores operational by Diwali and 10-12 by 31 March 2027; 8-10 NCR stores this financial year (two opening that week in Saket and Gurgaon, 3-4 under construction); about 5 South stores.

West Bengal capex of about INR 100 crore (plus or minus INR 5-10 crore) for stores plus about INR 50 crore for buying about 11 properties in Kolkata over the next two years, transactions possibly in Q1-Q2 FY28; all funded from internal accruals.

Per-store economics: about INR 2,500 per sq ft capex on a 10,000 sq ft store (about INR 2.5 crore) plus about INR 2 crore inventory; payback under 10-11 months in South and 16-18 months in North; breakeven 30-40 days in South and about 2-2.5 months in North.
Store opex targets: rent under 3% of revenue initially, manpower and marketing each under 1%, total store opex 8-10%; SSG targeted at 10-12% from year three.
Management said it will not commit to inorganic or rapid expansion and no franchise model; all stores are company-owned and company-operated on leased properties.
demand_pricing: Q1 FY27 SSG 34.2%; South cluster revenue +40% with 10.9% EBITDA margin; Andhra Pradesh revenue +62% (SSG 49.1%), Telangana up-country +48% (SSG 40%), Hyderabad city +34% (SSG 32.3%).
North cluster revenue +29% with 4.9% EBITDA margin; management said the North cooling-product market declined versus 2024, and Delhi NCR SSG was weak.

Management said the Andhra Pradesh AC unit volume was about 26,000-27,000 in the first six months against about 20,000 a year earlier with a similar store count; claimed market share gains of 4% to 12% in existing clusters outside Hyderabad.

543653|2026-03.headline: Bikaji Q4 FY26 revenue grew close to 18% to about INR720 crores, with FY26 revenue of INR2,994 crores and 9.5% volume growth.

For FY26, revenue was about INR2,994 crores on 9.5% volume growth, with consolidated gross margin of 35.1% and EBITDA margin of 13.7%, up over 120 bps. Q4 EBITDA was pressured by a step-up in advertising linked to the Bhujia and Kya Baat Hai Ji campaigns, plus a Bengal-election labour exodus and a 2.5-day factory shutdown. Management took a price rise of about 3% in April 2026 to offset edible oil and packaging inflation.
