rows.why: Realisations up 50% YoY to near INR300/kg; 60-70% of volume is long-term contracts, 30-35% spot, with some spot impact expected as China landed prices fell 30-40%.

rows.label: QVC salt order resumption
rows.why: QVC salt business still on hold due to Middle East conflict; a resumption would support the double-digit salt growth expected from Q3, but timing is not guided.

rows.label: Acume Chemicals derivatives reach break-even and build
rows.why: Derivatives first positive EBITDA of INR19m vs loss of INR27m a year ago, loss before tax narrowed to INR58.6m from INR103.3m, and utilisation is only ~40%.

tone.note: Management was confident on sequential margin gains, derivatives break-even, SiCSem and SOP timelines, but cautious on salt volumes and bromine power/shutdown losses, attributing the YoY decline to temporary logistics, fuel and power factors and pushing tests to Q2-Q3 FY27; analysts probed bromine v

543657|2026-09.headline: Archean Q2 FY27 standalone EBITDA rose 17.5% YoY to INR89.3 crore, but management withdrew SOP guidance and H1 EBITDA was flat.
543657|2026-09.overview: Standalone total income rose 32% YoY to INR305.4 crore and EBITDA rose 17.5% YoY to INR89.3 crore, with PAT of INR43.2 crore. Consolidated EBITDA for H1 fell 5.2% YoY to INR147.3 crore on a weak Q1. Bromine volumes and revenue grew strongly YoY, while industrial salt volumes fell 9% YoY and Acume posted a one-quarter EBITDA loss of about INR1 crore. Management cut the FY27 SOP volume outlook to 3,500-4,000 tons from 9,000-10,000 tons, and the Odisha semiconductor project (SiCSem) started civil works.

segments.name: Industrial salt
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR161 crore, up 9% YoY, with volumes down 9% YoY to about 812,000 tons because of customer deferrals tied to PVC and caustic soda. Management says H1 volume was about 1.8-1.9 million tons and it has high confidence in 4.2-4.3 million tons for FY27. Realisation was lifted by mix, and the cost per ton stayed flat QoQ.

segments.name: Bromine
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR127 crore, up 76% YoY. Volume was about 4,100 tons, up 29% YoY, and H1 volume was 8,300 tons, up 18% YoY. Realisation was up 36% YoY and stable QoQ. Unscheduled power cuts cost about 6-7% of output in the quarter.

segments.name: Acume (bromine derivatives)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR36 crore, up 81% YoY, with finished derivative volume of 2,115 tons, up 56% YoY. The quarter posted an EBITDA loss of about INR1 crore from adverse mix, one-time period costs and an inventory revaluation. H1 revenue was INR66 crore, up 51% YoY, and H1 was EBITDA positive. Capacity utilisation was about 40%.

segments.name: SOP (sulphate of potash)
segments.commentary: Q2 volume was 444 tons and value INR2.18 crore; H1 volume was about 2,400 tons. FY27 volume is now guided at 3,500-4,000 tons, versus the earlier 9,000-10,000 tons, because trials were delayed about a quarter and KTMS feedstock output was below plan.

guidance_outlook: FY27 bromine volume is expected at the lower end of the 18,000-20,000 ton guidance, with recovery of the 6-7% power-cut loss in H2.
FY27 salt volume is expected at 4.2-4.3 million tons, with an attempt to exceed 4.5 million tons. Management says the 4.5 million ton target has uncertainty.
Bromine average yield is expected to hold at about INR300/kg for the full year and at minimum each quarter.
SOP FY27 volume is cut to 3,500-4,000 tons. FY28 SOP throughput is expected to be significantly above this year, with pricing of USD 600-700/ton.
Management does not give earnings guidance. The Hajipir road re-routing (completed early October) is expected to mitigate most of the 15-30% increase in transport cost from Q3.
Bromine debottlenecking Phase 1 (25,000 tons run rate next year) is expected to finish in FY27. Flame retardant and the next bromine expansion are targeted for FY27-FY28 to FY28-FY29.

The Odisha semiconductor (SiCSem) project is about USD 240 million total, with a little under half funded by ISM. Management expects INR1,000-1,100 crore more investment, largely through debt, and 24 months of construction end to end.
Core chemical capex is to stay within the depreciation curve, with debt-to-equity of 0.6-0.7 (about 0.7 over three years).
capex_capacity: SiCSem project in Odisha: civil works started in Q2, environmental clearance received in mid-October, and first equipment consignments shipping. Construction is about 18-24 months; INR462.8 crore invested to date.

Brine field expansion: Phase 1 (4,000 hectares of an 8,000-hectare expansion, total 24,000 hectares) is in CWIP and expected to go live within about a quarter. Brine field expansion drives both salt and bromine volumes.
SOP plant modification is expected to be capitalised by end-FY27. Total CWIP is about INR120 crore, of which about INR80 crore is chemicals and about INR40 crore is SiCSem.
Bromine debottlenecking is on schedule, with some minor delays. Management expects completion in FY27.
Fleet: 100 new company-owned trailers were added in Q2 and a Kandla yard was commissioned. Electric trucks are at pilot stage, limited by charging downtime on about 300-400 km routes.
demand_pricing: Caustic soda and chlorine prices remain volatile. PVC demand is weak, with lower operating rates and deferrals from large salt customers; management expects a PVC price rebound this quarter.

Bromine exports are strong and pricing there is stable. Domestic bromine pricing is under pressure from agro and pharma slowdown and higher competitive intensity, which management says has not hit its own yields.

Industrial salt: about 80% of volume is on 18-24 month long-term contracts and about 10-20% is spot. Spot share has risen above 10% because of rescheduling. New export orders came from Vietnam and Oman.

Input inflation: industrial HSD rose from about INR87/litre in Q2 FY26 to about INR136 in Q2 FY27. Coal and propanol rose about 40% YoY, and sulphur more than doubled. Management expects cost pressure to continue through the rest of this year.
Oil and gas (oilfield specialty products at Oren Hydrocarbons): order traction is weak, with only campaign orders and no structured offtake. Management expects a ramp-up from Q1 FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Will bromine volume fall short of 18,000-20,000 tons, and will salt reach 4.5 million tons?
qa_highlights.answer: Bromine is expected at the lower end of guidance, with H2 recovery from power-cut losses of 6-7%. Salt is pegged at 4.2-4.3 million tons with an attempt to pass 4.5 million, and PVC-linked deferrals are the main uncertainty.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Hajipir road completion lift H2 EBITDA, and is there a risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said transport costs rose 15-30% from the diversions and that most of this should be mitigated from Q3. Risks are fuel prices (Q2 averaged about INR130 per litre, with further upside), winter recovery issues, and bromine volume.

qa_highlights.question: How much capex and debt will SiCSem need, and what is the timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: About USD 240 million total, of which a little under half is ISM-funded. Another INR1,000-1,100 crore is needed, largely debt, front-loaded. Interim construction milestones will be shared later.

qa_highlights.question: Why was SOP guidance cut and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: H1 SOP volume was about 2,400 tons. FY27 is now 3,500-4,000 tons because of a one-quarter trial delay and feedstock (KTMS) shortfalls. FY28 pricing is expected at USD 600-700/ton.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the Q2 salt realisation high?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to grade and geography mix, with more deferrals in lower-priced geographies. It said this was not a deliberate pricing change.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Acume operating rate and outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Finished production of 2,115 tons was about 40% of capacity. Management expects utilisation to rise over the next couple of quarters, though organic compound mix is weak.

risks_watch: Fuel and sulphur cost inflation, with management flagging that a further fuel increase could erode much of the logistics saving.
PVC-linked customer deferrals in salt, which could keep volumes below the 4.5 million ton target.
Power-cut downtime at bromine, and winter recovery issues.
The Hajipir land lease extension with the Gujarat government is still pending; management says there is no operational impact yet.
SOP feedstock (KTMS) and trial execution; FY28 volume and pricing remain unconfirmed.
Funding and execution risk on the SiCSem project (INR1,000-1,100 crore of debt-led funding, instrument not finalised).
543657|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on the bromine and road-logistics recovery, but cautious on salt volumes, fuel and sulphur costs, and SOP, where guidance was cut. Management declined to give earnings guidance and deferred several questions (Offgrid commercialisation, SOP FY28 volume, electric trucks) to later updates.
key_quotes: And we therefore do expect to see better throughput of volume and kind of improvement in cost structures with the starting of this new road, starting from this quarter onwards.
So we have downgraded that number given our feedstock condition, and the 1 quarter delay on the trials.
Sanjesh, we don't give guidance.
I think the semiconductor project will be around $240 million in terms of overall capital.

543663|2026-03.headline: Five-Star Q4 FY26: Q4 slippage fell to 0.7% from 1.9%, while FY27 AUM growth guided at ~20% and credit cost at 1.7-1.75%.
543663|2026-03.overview: Management described FY26 as the toughest year, with asset quality stress from MFI and unsecured overlap reaching the secured small-ticket LAP book. Q4 showed recovery: unique customer collection efficiency was 98.1%, x-bucket collections 99.3%, and slippage ratio fell to 0.7% from 1.9% in Q3. Disbursements rose 24% QoQ to INR1,213 crores and PAT was INR269 crores, down 3% QoQ on higher personnel expenses. Management guided to ~20% AUM growth in FY27 and a steady-state credit cost of 1.5-1.6% over FY28-30.

financial_highlights.change: management also cited 8.37% ROA on average AUM in the call
includes USD100mn ADB facility; USD50mn drawn

segments.name: South India (core)
segments.commentary: Around 85% or more of AUM is in the South, where over-leverage stress first appeared; management expects South to drive ~20% or more growth in FY27. Karnataka x-bucket collections were 99%.

segments.name: Non-South / new states
segments.commentary: Maharashtra operations started with branches in Nashik, Pune and Aurangabad, which lifted the Tier 1-2 share of AUM from ~1% to ~2%. Management plans to scale Maharashtra branches from ~40 to 70-80.

segments.name: Micro-LAP (INR3-5 lakh)
segments.commentary: Core product; management expects it to return to growth in a big way in FY27. Average ticket size rose from INR3.5 lakh to INR4.2 lakh YoY, and about 50%+ of AUM sits in INR3-5 lakh.

segments.name: Affordable housing
segments.commentary: Introduced in some locations, targeting INR7-8 lakh tickets. Management says it is a secondary priority behind micro-LAP.

guidance_outlook: FY27 AUM growth of around 20%, with a conservative range of 18-20%; management says close to 20% for the next two to three years.
FY27 disbursements of INR6,500-7,000 crores per the Q&A; another analyst's arithmetic used INR6,200-6,400 crores for 20% growth, which management said is achievable.
FY27 credit cost of 1.7-1.75% of average AUM; steady-state 1.5-1.6% for FY28-30.
FY27 opex to average AUM of 7-7.25%, with limited scale benefit.
FY27 ROA of 8.25-8.5% and steady-state ROA of 8-8.25%; spread around 13.5%.
Yield: about 30-40 bps further book-yield decline over the next 3-4 quarters; incremental lending at ~22.5%. Cost of funds: no major drop expected in FY27, with borrowing at ~8.5%.
Plan to open 60-75 branches in FY27, versus about 90-96 opened last year.
capex_capacity: Branch network: 60-75 new branches planned for FY27; 95% of branches opened last year have reached breakeven, per management.
Catchment area per branch of 25-30 km; new branches expected to break even in 9-12 months.
Business and collections teams separated and fully operational from April 1, 2026.
Write-offs for FY26 were about INR160-165 crores.
demand_pricing: April is seasonally weak; management says collections are in line with a typical April, and it expects no material deterioration.
Lead indicators are strong for disbursements; management expects Q1 FY27 disbursement growth.
Pricing was cut by 200 bps about 1.5 years ago; management sees no need to revise pricing in FY27 and expects no further cut.
Top-ups and repeat loans are 10-12% of disbursements. About 84% of Q4 collections were digital, up from 80% a year ago.
Management sees fintechs as a limited threat, given the INR4-5 lakh ticket size and roughly seven-year tenor against 6-12 months for fintech loans.
Exposure to small eateries and NRI remittance-linked borrowers is sub-1% of the portfolio, with no alarm signals so far.

qa_highlights.question: Credit cost trajectory for FY27 and steady state?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 guided at 1.7-1.75% (Q4 was 1.88%); steady state 1.5-1.6% for FY28-30, reflecting better buckets and a shift to slightly better-quality customers.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the steady-state credit cost higher than the earlier 0.8-1% guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Earlier guidance was on total assets (0.8-1%), roughly 1.3-1.35% on AUM. Management says it now expects to run at higher credit costs to avoid pressure on the field force while maintaining growth.

qa_highlights.question: Does the ROA outlook depend on margin given the steady-state credit cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided FY27 ROA of 8.25-8.5% and steady state of 8-8.25%. Leverage is currently low and will weigh on ROA but support ROE; spread is around 13.5%.

qa_highlights.question: Is Q4 personal expense a one-off?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called it a combination of collections-vertical build-out and seasonal Q4 incentives. It said this is business as usual, not a one-off, and added that the April increment will also add cost.

qa_highlights.question: Can AUM growth stay at ~20% beyond FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aims for close to 20% for the next two to three years, with an 18-20% range. Growth is to be supported by pent-up demand and a low base; FY27 AUM is expected to reach about INR16,000 crores.

qa_highlights.question: How much yield is left to reprice on the book?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects 30-40 bps more book-yield decline over 3-4 quarters. Incremental lending is at ~22.5%, book yield ~22-22.25%, and Q4 yield ~22.6%.

qa_highlights.question: What are the cost of funds and rating-upgrade expectations?
qa_highlights.answer: Excluding ADB, Q4 cost of funds was ~8.25-8.3%. Management expects FY27 borrowing at ~8.5% and no rating upgrade until the second half of the year, with about 30-40 bps more book-yield benefit over 2-3 years.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Stage-2 provision coverage below the RBI 5% norm a concern?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the ECL framework for banks starts April 2027 and does not expect the 5% Stage-2 norm for NBFCs soon. It is being conservative on credit cost and may see benefit if DPDs improve.

risks_watch: Stage-2 coverage fell as the 61-90 DPD bucket dropped from 5.1% to 4.8%; management tracks overall coverage instead.
Geopolitical stress (West Asia conflict) and liquidity in the borrowing market; management expects no major cost-of-funds benefit in FY27.
Disbursement ramp needs to rise from INR1,213 crores in Q4 to INR1,400-1,500 crores per quarter; April borrowing was zero given strong liquidity.
Senior management exit during FY26; management says there is no impact on performance.
Opex to AUM is guided at 7-7.25%, above historical levels, with competition for talent.
Rating upgrade is not expected until the second half of FY27 at the earliest.
543663|2026-03.management_tone: Confident and reassuring on collections, asset quality and growth, with repeated 'onwards and upwards' messaging. It was more cautious on cost of funds, liquidity and geopolitics, and evasive on the reason for a lower long-term growth rate versus the earlier ~25% framing.
key_quotes: I am very happy to state that the worst is behind us, and the coming quarters will see us moving in one direction: onwards and upwards.
So, structurally, 3 lakhs to 5 lakhs will be our core.
So, we don't really see a challenge getting to about INR 6,200 crores to INR6,400 crores of disbursements to achieve a 20% growth.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: 60-75 new branches are planned for FY27 versus about 90-96 opened last year, and Maharashtra branches are to scale from ~40 to 70-80.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: AUM growth guided at ~20% (18-20% conservative range) to about INR16,000 crore, and disbursements of INR6,500-7,000 crore versus INR4,675 crore in FY26, which needs quarterly disbursements to ramp from INR1,213 crore to INR1,400-1,500 crore.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade

rows.label: Q4 personnel cost build-out to persist
rows.why: Management said the Q4 personnel expense rise is business as usual, not a one-off, and the April increment adds cost; opex/AUM is guided at 7-7.25%, above historical levels.

rows.label: Book-yield decline of 30-40 bps over 3-4 quarters
rows.why: Book yield is ~22-22.25% against Q4 yield of ~22.6%, and incremental lending is at ~22.5%, so yield keeps compressing even though no further pricing cut is planned.

rows.why: Management said leverage is currently low and will weigh on ROA while supporting ROE; FY27 ROA is guided to 8.25-8.5%.

543663|2026-06.headline: Five-Star Q1 FY27 disbursements hit a record INR 1,496 crore (+23% QoQ, +16% YoY) while AUM grew 4% QoQ to INR 13,722 crore.
543663|2026-06.overview: Management reported a record quarterly disbursement of INR 1,496 crore and AUM of INR 13,722 crore, up 4% QoQ. Asset quality metrics improved modestly: 1+ current book rose to 83.30%, 30+ fell to 12.38%, and the 1.85% credit cost was slightly lower QoQ, while slippages were flat at 0.70%. Management guided to lower credit costs and NPLs in coming quarters, with opex staying flat in FY27 on an employee-cost reset. Q&A focused on yield compression, cost of borrowing, write-off run-rate, opex, and the timeline to higher leverage.

financial_highlights.change: Average cost of funds down ~15 bps, spread up 3 bps
Recoveries ~INR 35 crore incl. write-off and NPA settlements (vs INR 26-27 crore in Q4)

segments.name: Micro LAP (core product)
segments.commentary: Onboarding yields average ~22.5% (range 21.5%-23%); management sees yield settling near 22.25% after 10-15 bps further compression over next couple of quarters. Average ticket size ~INR 4.5-5 lakh, targeting 25/50/25 mix across ~INR 3 lakh, ~INR 5 lakh and ~INR 10 lakh tickets.

segments.name: Housing loans
segments.commentary: Launched about two quarters ago; management said focus has been on restoring micro LAP before pushing housing.

guidance_outlook: FY27 AUM growth guidance of ~20% reiterated; management expects FY27 disbursements of INR 6,500-6,800 crore (Q1 run-rate plus ~10%).
FY27 credit cost guided at 1.7%-1.9%; management said the trend is more likely toward 1.7%. Overall ECL coverage to be maintained at ~1.75%-1.8%.
Gross NPA to fall to sub-3% and a steady-state NPA of ~2.5%; steady-state Stage 1 ~91-92%, Stage 2 ~6-7%.
Write-offs for FY27 guided at INR 225-250 crore (~INR 55-60 crore per quarter).
Opex to stay largely flat in FY27 with 20-21% YoY growth; cost-to-assets ~5.75%-6% in FY27, moving to 5.25%-5.5% from FY28. Branch additions run-rate ~50-60 per year.
Incremental cost of borrowing guided at ~8.5%; spreads expected flat for next few quarters absent policy action. Repo rate increases are a downside risk.
FY28 credit cost expected at ~1.6%-1.7%. Debt-to-equity of 2x expected in 6-8 quarters; ROA steady state 6%-6.5% and ROE 18%-20% at ~3x leverage.
Management plans to launch one more product (beyond micro LAP and housing) within ~3-6 months, with details to be shared later.
capex_capacity: Branch network at ~856 after adding ~12 in Q1, mainly in Maharashtra and newer states; FY27 additions expected at ~50-60 branches.
Collections and business functions separated into different verticals; management says this lifted productivity without any change in credit filters.
Liquidity: ~INR 1,850 crore held on balance sheet at quarter end; ~INR 1,000 crore raised in Q4 and ~INR 450 crore raised in Q1.
Pending ADB tranche (ECB) to be raised, with hedging cost impact; timing to be managed.
demand_pricing: Management says demand was never the constraint; the slowdown over the past 3-4 quarters came from tighter approvals and deliberate disbursement pacing.
June disbursements were ~INR 670 crore; management expects a new normal of ~INR 600-650 crore per month on average, with intra-quarter seasonality being reduced.
Repeat-customer policy relaxed: top-up offered to best customers instead of requiring full prepayment, which management expects to reduce the repayment rate from ~30% toward 27-28%.
Microfinance overlap with Five-Star customers fell from ~20-21% to ~16-17% (per management, not measured for Q1).
Competition: management cited new competitors entering, requiring more competitive employee compensation.

qa_highlights.question: Renish (ICICI): Where will cost-to-assets settle and when does operating leverage kick in?
qa_highlights.answer: Opex to stay largely flat in FY27 with 20-21% YoY growth due to competitive employee pay; cost-to-assets ~5.75%-6% this year, moving to 5.25%-5.5% in steady state from FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Renish: Has yield repricing largely finished, and what is the current lending rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Large part of contraction done; onboarding yields average ~22.5% (range 21.5%-23%); a further 10-15 bps compression expected over next couple of quarters, settling near 22.25% after NPA interest reversals.

qa_highlights.question: Viral Shah (IIFL): Further Stage 3 flow-through expected, any ARC sales, and rollback rates in early buckets?
qa_highlights.answer: No ARC sales. Slippages expected to trend down; recoveries ~INR 35 crore vs INR 26-27 crore in Q4. Rollbacks ~4-5% in 1-60 DPD buckets and ~2-3% in 61-90 DPD; management frames it as stabilisation, with unique customer collection efficiency key.

qa_highlights.question: Abhijit Tibrewal (Motilal Oswal): How many more quarters until slippages decline and what is a normalised slippage rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Expects slippages, credit cost and NPLs to trend down in September, December and March quarters; credit cost trending toward 1.7%. Will wait 1-2 quarters of slippage trend before giving a steady-state slippage number.

qa_highlights.question: Abhijit: What drives the disbursement acceleration (demand, approvals, productivity, geography)?
qa_highlights.answer: Demand was never the constraint; earlier slowdown reflected tighter approvals and deliberate pacing. Vertical split of business and collections lifted productivity with no change in credit filters; login and sanction traction strong.

qa_highlights.question: Abhijit: What is the outlook for cost of borrowing?
qa_highlights.answer: Incremental cost of borrowing ~8.5%, leaving room for 20-30 bps further compression on the book; pending ADB ECB tranche carries hedging cost; assumes no repo hikes.

qa_highlights.question: Chandrasekhar Sridhar (Fidelity): Is gold loan growth masking underlying stress via repayments by overlapping customers? Also ticket size and diversification?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says gold loans are fully secured and repayments via gold loans are seasonal; microfinance overlap down from ~20-21% to ~16-17% (not measured for Q1). Ticket size mix target 25/50/25 across ~INR 3 lakh, 5 lakh, 10 lakh; one more product within 3-6 months. Spreads to stay flat for next few quarters absent policy action.

qa_highlights.question: Raghav Garg (Ambit): Why have repayment rates risen, and how does that reconcile with a rising 3-5 year duration share?
qa_highlights.answer: Repayments rose on stronger collections and a policy change: top-up offered to best customers instead of full prepayment. Repayment rate currently ~30%, expected to trend to 27-28%; behavioural tenor ~4-4.5 years. Management said 85-90% of loans are disbursed on 7-year tenure; the vintage shift reflects seasoning and higher disbursements.

qa_highlights.question: Rajiv Mehta (Yes Securities): Trajectory of write-offs, coverage build-back, and FY28 credit cost?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 write-offs guided INR 225-250 crore, roughly flat at ~INR 55-60 crore per quarter; steady-state write-off view in 2-3 quarters. Overall ECL coverage ~1.75-1.8%, whichever mix of Stage 1/2/3. FY28 credit cost ~1.6-1.7%. Growth achieved with no change in credit filters.

qa_highlights.question: Kunal Shah (Citi): Steady-state bucket mix and employee cost drivers, attrition?
qa_highlights.answer: Steady state: Stage 1 ~91-92%, Stage 2 ~6-7%, Stage 3 ~2.5%; current book to reach ~85% by end FY27 from 83.3%; 30+ below 12%. Employee cost rise is salary realignment and incentives for branch staff, not ESOPs. Attrition flat so far; trends in 2-3 quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Nischint (Kotak): Expense growth this year and whether 20% loan growth guidance stands?
qa_highlights.answer: Opex growth ~20-21% YoY, similar to Q1; increments and appraisals already in Q1 base. ECL coverage ~1.75-1.8%; write-offs INR 55-60 crore per quarter; 20% AUM growth guidance reconfirmed.

qa_highlights.question: Divyansh Gupta (Latent PMS): Why did debt decline from March, cost of funds for levering up, and timing of D/E of 2x?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 borrowing was muted as banks awaited results; INR 1,000 crore raised in Q4 and INR 450 crore in Q1; INR 1,850 crore liquidity held. Guide 8.5% incremental cost. D/E of 2x in 6-8 quarters, as net worth adds ~INR 1,100-1,200 crore PAT annually.

qa_highlights.question: Chirag Fialoke (MS Capital): Are incremental disbursements averaging INR 5-7 lakh, and what is the 60-90 DPD bucket?
qa_highlights.answer: Average ticket ~INR 4.5-5 lakh, expected to hold around INR 5 lakh; mix guidance unchanged. Management deferred the 60-90 DPD figure to the IR team.

qa_highlights.question: Darshan Deora (Indvest): Steady-state ROE target, and will yields be raised back given higher collection costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Current ROA ~8-8.5% on AUM (7-7.25% on total assets); steady-state ROA 6-6.5% and ROE 18-20% at ~3x leverage. Management says the cost increase will be recovered through lower credit cost, not higher lending rates; the 200 bps cut in Oct 2024 tracked borrowing costs falling from 11%+.

qa_highlights.question: Renish: What was June disbursement and is INR 600-650 crore a monthly run-rate?
qa_highlights.answer: June disbursements ~INR 670 crore; management is working to reduce intra-quarter seasonality and agreed an average of ~INR 600-650 crore per month is a fair assumption for the rest of the year.

risks_watch: Yield compression: onboarding yields ~22.5% with a further 10-15 bps decline expected over the next couple of quarters, and NPA interest reversals weigh on yields.

Cost of borrowing: guidance of ~8.5% incremental assumes no repo hikes; a rate increase or ADB ECB hedging costs would hit spreads. Management flagged energy costs and possible regulatory liquidity moves.

Asset quality: slippages flat QoQ at 0.70%; credit cost guidance 1.7-1.9% and gross NPA sub-3% depend on slippages turning down in September, December and March quarters. Write-off run-rate ~INR 60 crore per quarter gives little relief in FY27.
Opex and employee cost: opex growth 20-21% YoY and cost-to-assets ~5.75-6% in FY27; attrition is flat and too early to call, with more competitors entering.
Disbursement sustainability: H1 run-rate of ~INR 600-650 crore per month and reliance on a new product within 3-6 months; leverage target of 2x D/E is 6-8 quarters away.
key_quotes: We clocked our historical best in disbursement with quarterly disbursements coming in at INR 1,496 crores, a growth of 23% over the previous quarter and 16% over the previous year.
So our request is, can you please keep yourself mute so that the background noise is too much.
So it's not like we are completely removing the DNA of collections from the business people.
Srikanth Gopalakrishnan: Interest reversals on NPAs, Renish.
543663|2026-06.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on disbursements, collections and asset-quality direction, but cautious on the near-term outlook: management hedged on borrowing costs, energy and rate risks, and deferred several data questions (rollback, 60-90 DPD, collection efficiency) to the IR team.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Onboarding yields ~22.5% with a further 10-15 bps compression expected, cost of funds down only ~15 bps and spreads guided flat, so NIM expansion from here is limited; credit cost relief is the main lever, with cost-to-assets flat at ~5.75-6% in FY27.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.when: FY27 (50-60 branches over the year, ~12 added in Q1)
rows.why: Branch network at ~856 after ~12 additions in Q1, with 50-60 more planned for FY27 as a run-rate of ~50-60 per year, so branch capacity keeps coming online through the window.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: FY27 disbursement guidance of INR 6,500-6,800 crore (Q1 run-rate plus ~10%) and AUM growth ~20% reiterated; June at ~INR 670 crore and a new normal of INR 600-650 crore per month, with AUM at INR 13,722 crore (+4% QoQ) only partly reflecting the pickup.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Credit cost trending toward 1.7% (low end of 1.7-1.9%) and disbursements at a record INR 1,496 crore, with June at ~INR 670 crore, could support upside if slippages fall as management expects.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Incremental borrowing cost guided at ~8.5% with spreads flat and no repo hikes assumed, while slippages at 0.70% flat QoQ must turn down in Sep, Dec and Mar quarters for the 1.7-1.9% credit cost guide to hold; rate hikes or ADB ECB hedging costs are the named risks.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.when: within ~3-6 months of the call (roughly Q2-Q3 FY27)
rows.why: Management plans one more product beyond micro LAP and housing within 3-6 months, with details to follow; housing launched about two quarters ago.

rows.label: Move to 2x D/E
rows.why: Management expects D/E of 2x in 6-8 quarters as net worth adds ~INR 1,100-1,200 crore PAT annually; net worth is INR 7,653 crore at 30 June, with ~INR 1,850 crore liquidity on balance sheet.

rows.label: Asset quality stabilisation
rows.why: Management expects slippages, credit cost and NPLs to trend down in these quarters; current book at 83.30% (vs 82.69% in Q4) to reach ~85% by end FY27, and 30+ DPD at 12.38% (vs 12.69%).

rows.label: No yield re-pricing up
rows.why: Management says higher collection costs will be recovered via lower credit cost, not higher lending rates; onboarding yields ~22.5% with 10-15 bps further compression expected.

tone.note: Management was confident on record disbursements, collections and the asset-quality direction, but cautious on borrowing costs, energy and rate risks, and deferred rollback, 60-90 DPD and collection-efficiency questions to the IR team; analysts pushed on yield compression, cost of borrowing, write-o

543663|2026-09.headline: Five-Star Q2 FY27: record disbursements of Rs 2,078 crore (+74% YoY) and PAT of Rs 299 crore, but management flags spread compression ahead.
543663|2026-09.overview: Disbursements hit a historical high of Rs 2,078 crore, up 39% QoQ and 74% YoY, while AUM reached Rs 14,640 crore (+14% YoY). Collection efficiency improved to 98.2% and 30+ DPD fell to 11.5% from 12.38%, though GNPA was sticky at 3.48%. PAT was Rs 299 crore, including a Rs 19 crore one-time tax benefit (about Rs 281 crore underlying). Management guided to tighter spreads as cost of funds rises, partly offset by a roughly 1% yield hike on incremental loans effective October 2026.

financial_highlights.value: Rs 299 crore (Rs 281 crore excluding Rs 19 crore one-time tax benefit)
about 7.5% in Q2; about 7.35-7.40% for the year

segments.name: Core geographies (Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana)
segments.commentary: Together more than 80% of AUM; management reports no drought-like stress and collections holding up. Tamil Nadu collects best, followed by Andhra and Telangana.

segments.name: Karnataka
segments.commentary: Management says collections are improving month-on-month after the state ordinance impact, and disbursements are being pushed more firmly there.

segments.name: Ticket-size mix (disbursements)
segments.commentary: Sub Rs 3 lakh about 26-27%, Rs 3-5 lakh about 51-52%, above Rs 5 lakh the balance. Target steady state is about 25/50/25.

guidance_outlook: Expect flattish credit slippages and credit cost for the rest of FY27; slippage around 70 bps for the next couple of quarters.
Incremental yields up about 1% from October 2026, but absorbing it across the book will take roughly 24-36 months (about 8 quarters per management on one question).
Incremental cost of borrowings expected 8.70-8.75% in H2 FY27; book cost of funds to exit FY27 about 12-15 bps higher, near 8.90%.
Spread compression expected: about 10-12 bps for H1 and about 10-15 bps by FY27 exit; margin expansion ruled out.
Growth guidance to be comfortably exceeded; any revised guidance likely after Q3. Opex to AUM to fall 50-75 bps over the next couple of years, to 6.75-7%.
October disbursements about Rs 550 crore (muted), with November and December expected to pick up.
capex_capacity: Added 19 branches in Q2 and 75 over the last year, focused on deepening presence in core geographies.
Active loans about 5.1 lakh, up 5% YoY.
Liquidity about Rs 1,300 crore at September 30; unavailed sanctions about Rs 1,100 crore.
Raised incremental debt of Rs 825 crore at an all-in cost of 8.43%; bank borrowings about 69% of total (67% in Q1).
Second tranche of ADB facility still pending, with hedging cost on the higher side.
demand_pricing: Customer rates raised about 1% on incremental disbursements across risk categories, from about 21-23% to about 22.5-23.9%, effective October 2026.
Top-up loans are about 10-15% of disbursements (Rs 200-300 crore per quarter); incremental top-up disbursal about 50% of the outstanding.
Management says yield hikes will not raise defaults, citing that loans above Rs 5 lakh earlier carried the same yield as sub-Rs 3 lakh loans.
Insurance commission impact from the IRDAI circular is nil, as Five-Star passes insurance premiums through without earning commission.
Gold loan overlap: 40-50% of customers have some gold loan; meaningful overlap about 30-40%.

qa_highlights.question: How will asset quality move given the rainfall deficit, and any stress signs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management sees no drought stress in core states; collections in October are in line with July and September, with October D1C1 expected near 98%.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the repayment rate rising, and what is the behavioural tenure?
qa_highlights.answer: Repayment rises due to adjusting outstanding on internal top-ups (about 1-2% extra repayments); behavioural tenure to move closer to 4 years, from the 36-37% repayment rate.

qa_highlights.question: How much have customer rates been raised, and when does yield bottom?
qa_highlights.answer: About 1% on incremental disbursements; management agreed that yields have bottomed this quarter, but margin expansion is not expected.

qa_highlights.question: What drives the write-off recovery trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Recoveries take about 18-24 months given no SARFAESI access on loans below Rs 20 lakh; H1 recoveries were about Rs 20 crore and NPA resolutions Rs 35 crore in Q2 (Rs 25 crore in Q1).

qa_highlights.question: How will cost of funds and spread move?
qa_highlights.answer: Incremental cost of borrowing to rise 20-25 bps vs Q2, with book cost up 12-15 bps by FY27 exit; H1 spread hit about 10-12 bps, roughly 8 bps post-tax.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the rise in other expenses?
qa_highlights.answer: Legal expenses from the scaled-up legal recovery vertical and CSR spend based on the 3-year average profit.

risks_watch: Rate cycle: a further 25-50 bp repo hike would add to cost of funds beyond the 10-15 bps built in; December policy is a key watch point.
Stage-3 at 3.48%, with Stage-3 rising about 7-8% in absolute terms; management expects a trend-down only in a couple of quarters.
61-90 DPD bucket slippages flat, leaving a sticky stock in the bucket that drives the 70 bps slippage run-rate.
Written-off pool recovery slow (about Rs 300 crore written off in the last 8 quarters vs Rs 150 crore earlier); management has agreed to consider more disclosure.
MFI exposure about 35-40% of customers and no fresh scrub done; a sector relapse would test the collections set-up.
Revised guidance to come only after Q3; new product line still undisclosed, with details promised next quarter.
543663|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on growth, collections and operating momentum, with repeated use of phrases like 'historical best'. Cautious and specific on spreads, GNPA stickiness and recovery timing, and evasive on specific AUM growth targets.
key_quotes: Our upward trajectory in disbursements continued during the current quarter as well, where we recorded our historical best disbursement of Rs. 2,078 crores, up 39% over previous quarter and 74% year -on-year.
We expect flattish credit slippages and credit cost for the rest of the year, despite the industry headwinds.
No, margin expansion is not possible , Nischint, because we are already seeing the effect of the repo rate increase on our existing borrowings.
Our book is fixed. So, we will not be able to change the rate on the existing book. Fresh disbursements will come in at 1% higher yields.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Spread compression of 10-12 bps in H1 and 10-15 bps by FY27 exit as incremental cost of borrowing rises to 8.70-8.75% against a ~1% yield hike on incremental loans; management explicitly rules out margin expansion.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: 19 branches added in Q2 and 75 over the last year, with continued deepening in core geographies; no quantified capacity plan beyond branch rollout, so call is likely rather than surely.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Disbursements hit Rs 2,078 crore (+74% YoY) and AUM is up 14% YoY to Rs 14,640 crore, though October disbursements are muted at about Rs 550 crore with a pick-up expected in November and December.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: AUM growth guided to comfortably cross earlier guidance, with any revised guidance possibly after Q3; record Rs 2,078 crore disbursements (+74% YoY) back this up.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Management expects flattish credit cost and slippage around 70 bps, and says AUM growth will comfortably exceed earlier guidance; the risk is spread compression of 10-15 bps by FY27 exit rather than a guidance cut.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: A new product line is undisclosed, with details promised next quarter; no size or timing beyond that.

rows.label: 1% yield hike on incremental loans from October 2026
rows.why: Customer rates raised about 1% on incremental disbursements (from about 21-23% to 22.5-23.9%), but absorbing it across the book will take roughly 24-36 months, so it only partly offsets cost-of-funds rise.

rows.label: Rate-cycle risk to cost of funds
rows.why: A further 25-50 bp repo hike would add to cost of funds beyond the 10-15 bps already built in; book cost of funds exits FY27 near 8.90% versus 8.78% now.

rows.label: Opex to AUM decline
rows.when: over the next couple of years
rows.why: Opex to AUM guided to fall 50-75 bps to 6.75-7% from about 7.35-7.40% for FY27, though Q2 ran at about 7.5%.

tone.note: Management was confident on record disbursements, collections and growth, and cautious and specific on spread compression, sticky GNPA and slow recoveries; analysts probed the rate cycle, asset quality stress and yield timing.

543664|2026-03.headline: Kaynes FY26 revenue rose 33.2% to INR3,626 crore, but missed the INR4,500 crore then INR4,000 crore guidance, with operating cash flow of about INR600 crore negative.
543664|2026-03.overview: Management attributed the revenue shortfall to West Asia-related customer deferments, supply chain delays and one large EV two-wheeler customer cutting volumes by about 90%. Consolidated FY26 EBITDA was INR5,741 million (15.8% margin) and PAT INR3,639 million (10% margin), with Q4 revenue of INR12,426 million (+26% YoY) and PAT of INR912 million. Cash flow weakened sharply, driven by the smart metering subsidiary (Iskraemeco) with receivables of about INR1,365 crore, while the standalone EMS business turned cash positive. Management declined to give a specific FY27 revenue number and instead guided to outgrowing the market at roughly twice the market growth rate.

financial_highlights.change: PBT hit by about INR32 crore of quarterly intangible amortisation
from 83 days FY24; management also cited 64 to 54 days

segments.name: EMS (standalone/KEMPL)
segments.commentary: FY26 EMS revenue about INR2,655 crore (Q1 INR442 crore, Q2 INR683 crore, Q3 INR667 crore, Q4 INR862 crore), growing about 26-30%. Standalone EMS operating cash flow INR250 crore positive versus INR65 crore last year; EMS receivables INR399 crore at year end versus INR379 crore at start.

segments.name: Smart metering (Iskraemeco subsidiary)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue about INR971 crore (roughly 24-25% of group revenue), with receivables about INR1,365 crore, of which about INR250 crore non-current. Installation delays in rural areas and state-government/DISCOM payment cycles are holding up collections; securitisation has discounted only about INR40 crore so far.

segments.name: OSAT
segments.commentary: Unit 1 fully operational; Unit 2 to commercialise by Q2 FY27. Management cites revenue visibility above INR25,000 million over five years. Sanand facility inaugurated by the Prime Minister; FY27 production estimate INR250-300 crore, export-oriented.

segments.name: PCB
segments.commentary: Management sees a confirmed demand pipeline for five years with customers seeking more capacity. FY27 production estimate INR300-400 crore; first year of operation.

segments.name: Rail (Kavach)
segments.commentary: Kavach has initial approval and trial orders; approvals expected in H1 FY27, with bulk orders in H2. Management expects rail revenue to grow about 20-25% with margins above 30%.

segments.name: EV / automotive
segments.commentary: EV segment grew about 28% in FY26 despite the large two-wheeler customer falling about 90%. Company is moving from PCB supply into assemblies and products.

guidance_outlook: No explicit FY27 revenue number; management guides to growing at about twice the market rate (market cited at 15-18% EMS growth), with quarterly updates on market versus Kaynes growth.
Standalone EMS to stay cash positive, with working capital days improving by about 8-10 days in the coming years.
Consolidated operating cash flow: management expects the INR600 crore negative to fall by 70-80% by Q3 FY27 and turn positive by year end.
Metering receivables and installation expected to be completed within about 3 quarters; the business will move to an EMS-component-only model for new orders.
Target of NPD-led and value-added revenue at nearly 30% of total revenue over the coming years.
Smart meter FY27 revenue expected roughly flat to slightly up or down versus INR971 crore, with about 50% of volume on the old model and about 50% on the new model.
Quarterly amortisation of acquired intangibles (Iskraemeco and August Electronics, about INR320 crore) going forward, after the Q4 catch-up of about INR32 crore.
capex_capacity: OSAT Unit 1 fully operational; Unit 2 to commercialise by Q2 FY27 (Sanand facility inaugurated by the Prime Minister).
FY26 intangibles rose to INR536 crore from INR238 crore, mainly from acquisitions of Iskraemeco and August Electronics (Canada, North America EMS), with about INR320 crore capitalised.
Mysore facility crossed INR10,000 million revenue in FY26.
Metering: about 35 lakh meters on current order, plus a possible 3.5-4 lakh-meter extension; 2-3 months needed to complete pending supply, with installation taking 1-2 quarters more.
Launched three products now in production (SOP started), and a 9-month product launch cycle versus 12-18 months previously.
Investing in NPD engineering, co-development, digital and R&D infrastructure, and predictive maintenance / Industry 4.0 at 2 plants.
demand_pricing: Order book above INR9,000 crore, described as diversified and non-cancellable; management says there is no structural deterioration in demand.
Q4 and FY26 shortfall attributed to West Asia conflict, last-minute customer deferments, supply chain delays and product timing shifts; some revenue recognition shifted though orders remain valid.
Auto industry outlook cut from mid-double-digit growth (December projection) to single-digit or low double-digit, per management, which raised caution on offtake.
Aerospace, railway, defence, space and EV are being added to reduce dependence on any one vertical.
OSAT and PCB output expected to be export-oriented at first; internal versus external consumption still being decided.

qa_highlights.question: Viral Shah: What is the sanctity of guidance given the INR4,500 crore then INR4,000 crore targets versus about INR3,600 crore actual, and the OCF miss?
qa_highlights.answer: Management apologised, said the INR4,500 crore target implied about 55% growth, and blamed a large EV two-wheeler customer dropping about 90% of volume plus government project delays. On OCF, it said standalone EMS was cash positive at INR250 crore while the metering business drove the consolidated outflow.

qa_highlights.question: Nitin Arora: Why no guidance, and what will move the INR600 crore negative OCF to breakeven?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it now commits to outgrowing the market at twice market growth rather than a number. It expects the INR600 crore negative to fall 70-80% by Q3 FY27 and turn positive by year end, with metering installations the key lever.

qa_highlights.question: Renu Baid Pugalia: Share of metering in revenue, growth ex-metering, rail ramp-up and government-offtake risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Metering is about 20-25% of revenue, but about 60% of that business was already EMS supply. EV grew about 28%. Kavach has initial approval and trial orders, with H1 approvals and H2 bulk orders expected; rail growth of 20-25% is targeted.

qa_highlights.question: Amber Singhania: Metering subsidiary revenue, EBITDA and receivables; why receivables rose despite the securitisation plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Metering revenue was INR971 crore and receivables about INR1,365 crore. Securitisation has only started with one bank, with about INR40 crore discounted in each of two quarters, because the bank needs first-month billing and collections; installation delays are the main constraint.

qa_highlights.question: Dhaval Somaiya: Pending meter count, and breakup of the other roughly INR740 crore of subsidiary revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Pending supply to be completed in 2-3 months, with a possible 3.5-4 lakh-meter extension. Of the EMS revenue of INR2,655 crore, two foreign entities contributed about INR300 crore on average, and KEMPL is the main EMS subsidiary.

qa_highlights.question: Sumant Kumar: Why did intangibles rise by about INR300 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Acquisitions of Iskraemeco and August Electronics capitalised about INR320 crore of intangibles. Amortisation was booked once in Q4 (about INR32 crore), and will now be booked quarterly.

qa_highlights.question: Achal Lohade: Do the INR1,000 crore OSAT and INR500 crore PCB production targets still stand?
qa_highlights.answer: Ramesh Kunhikannan said no such guidance was given. He estimated FY27 PCB output at INR300-400 crore and OSAT at INR250-300 crore, both export-led.

risks_watch: Receivables and cash flow: metering receivables of about INR1,365 crore, of which about INR250 crore non-current; securitisation has discounted only about INR80 crore cumulatively.
Guidance credibility: the company missed its INR4,500 crore then INR4,000 crore revenue targets, and the CFO was unavailable for the call due to health reasons.
Top management restructuring and role realignment flagged during the quarter.
Customer concentration: a large EV two-wheeler customer fell about 90%.
Government payment and installation dependency for smart metering; DISCOM and GENCO timelines.
Quarterly amortisation of acquired intangibles now recurs (about INR32 crore per quarter), which will depress PAT.
Auto industry outlook downgraded; OSAT and PCB ramp and internal versus external sales mix still undecided.

rows.label: Volume growth

rows.why: Capex was not discussed directly; FY26 intangibles rose to INR536 crore from INR238 crore mainly through acquisitions, and utilisation was not disclosed, so a fresh capex announcement is conditional on OSAT/PCB ramp and cash flow recovering.

rows.why: Operating cash flow was about INR600 crore negative against marginally negative guidance, metering receivables are about INR1,365 crore with only about INR80 crore securitised, and auto outlook was cut to single-digit or low double-digit growth.

rows.why: Management expects the INR600 crore negative OCF to fall 70-80% by Q3 FY27 and turn positive by year end, with metering installations and collections as the key lever; metering receivables are about INR1,365 crore.

rows.why: Standalone EMS working capital days fell to 53 from 83 in FY24 and standalone EMS was cash positive at INR250 crore versus INR65 crore last year.

543664|2026-06.headline: Kaynes Q1 FY27 revenue rose 40% to INR946 crore and EBITDA rose 31% to INR147.6 crore, but operating cash flow was negative INR259 crore as inventory and metering receivables rose.
543664|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 40% YoY to INR946 crore, driven by EMS (standalone EMS up 53%, overseas up 327% on the August Electronics acquisition), while smart metering fell 12% YoY to about INR204 crore as management deliberately curbed supplies over collections. EBITDA was INR147.6 crore at a 15.6% margin, with management flagging margin pressure from component and PCB cost inflation and lead times of 6 to 8 months. Negative operating cash flow was about INR259 crore (management also cited INR235 crore in another bridge), with inventory up about INR177 crore and receivables up about INR68 crore. OSAT and PCB commissioning remains guided for Q3 FY27, with a FY27 revenue target of INR450 to 500 crore across both.

segments.name: EMS (overall, incl. overseas)
segments.commentary: Revenue of INR854 crore including GST, with 40% overall EMS growth and about 48% growth cited by management; collections of INR847 crore. Receivables in EMS were about INR613 crore at quarter end versus INR606 crore at the start.

segments.name: Smart metering (GridCrest)
segments.commentary: Sales about INR240 crore including GST against collections of INR88 crore, so production and supply were halted. Metering receivables rose from INR1,158 crore to INR1,311 crore; about INR200 crore was received in early July.

segments.name: OSAT (Kaynes Semicon)
segments.commentary: Capex to date about INR700 crore; government subsidy of INR170 crore received till July 2026. Commercial billing expected from Q3 FY27; Unit 2 on track for operation by Q3 FY27. Mitsui partnership for Japan access announced.

segments.name: PCB (Kaynes Circuit)
segments.commentary: Capex to date about INR500 crore, with about INR250 crore in transit. Commercial production to start next quarter; one global customer has requested the entire capacity and trials are ongoing with a vendor code approved.

guidance_outlook: Revenue growth committed at 2x the market growth; no absolute top-line number given. Market grew about 17% in Q1.
OSAT and PCB combined FY27 revenue target INR450 to 500 crore, with revenue starting from Q3 FY27.
FY27 capex plan: about INR300 crore OSAT, about INR300 crore PCB and about INR250 crore EMS; Q1 spend about INR230 crore in total across these.
Management expects profitability to take a couple of quarters to normalise; FY27 described as a difficult, tough year.
Management expects receivables turnaround in the metering business and cash-positive position by end of FY27.
Working capital to be reported on a rolling 12-month basis going forward.
capex_capacity: Q1 FY27 capex about INR180 crore (per management in the call), against a broader plan of about INR300 crore each for OSAT and PCB and about INR250 crore for EMS.

Kaynes Semicon Unit 2 and Kaynes Circuit Chennai remain on track to be operational by Q3 FY27, despite minor slippage from West Asia-related equipment and logistics disruption.

Component prices up about 30% to 35% per management; PCB prices up about 3x; lead times more than 6 to 8 months in some categories; PCB suppliers demanding advance payment.
FX impact on imports about 3.3% of import level, per management.
Pass-through to customers is on a quarter-on-quarter basis and may lag; management said agreements with strategic customers allow some price pass-through.
Aerospace recovered in the quarter; management said growth was seen across railways, automotive, aerospace and defence.

543686|2026-03.headline: Sirca Q4 FY26 revenue rose 33.07% YoY to INR134.29 crore and FY26 EBITDA margin reached 20.08%, with management guiding 25-30% growth and 19-21% EBITDA margin for FY27.
543686|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 standalone revenue grew 33.07% YoY to INR134.29 crore, EBITDA rose 35.69% to INR25.74 crore (margin 19.17% vs 18.8%), and PAT rose 25.07% to INR17.71 crore. For FY26, revenue was INR492.48 crore (+31.79%), EBITDA INR98.88 crore (+46.62%) and PAT INR65.05 crore (+32.48%). Management flagged short-term raw material margin pressure from crude-linked inputs, offset by two price increases totalling about 10% on Sirca range, and a March NC raw material shortage that cost Wembley about INR4-5 crore of revenue. The company has shifted from pure trading to manufacturing, with about 95% of previously imported products now targeted for Indian production.

segments.name: Core Sirca wood coatings
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue of about INR372 crore, of which about INR124 crore came from Italy-imported products and about INR252 crore from products made in India. Sirca gross margins are higher than Wembley/Welcome by about 10-15 percentage points.

segments.name: Wembley and Welcome (acquired brands, mass segment)
segments.commentary: Combined FY26 revenue of about INR120.5 crore: Welcome about INR46.5 crore and Wembley about INR74 crore. Wembley was roughly flat YoY after INR4-5 crore of orders were lost in March to an NC raw material shortage, and about INR5-6 crore was billed to distributors before the acquisition closed.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: FY25 exports were about INR9 crore, mainly Nepal plus one or two Sri Lanka customers. Wembley Valentino polyurethane exports are expected to start in Q1 FY27, with management targeting exports of about 3-4% of revenue.

segments.name: Acrylic coatings (Sirca brand)
segments.commentary: Acrylic sales contributed about INR120 crore in FY26 per management. Made-in-India production is expected to roll out in Q1 FY27 after the December 2025 know-how transfer from Sirca Italy.

EBITDA margin guided to stay in the 19-21% range, with raw material pressure expected to be temporary after two price increases.
Management said the INR1,000 crore revenue vision is achievable in about three years (FY29) and that Sirca and Wembley capacities are broadly sufficient for that journey.
FY27 capex limited to about INR5-6 crore, mainly for acrylic production expansion.
Expects inventory to fall by about INR15-20 crore and debtors to decline in the coming quarters as import stock is consumed by June end.
Expects NC supply constraints from supplier Nitrex to ease from June with a new Nitrex unit starting operations.
Expects exports to Middle East including Dubai to begin in FY27, and export contribution of about 3-4% of revenue.
capex_capacity: Sirca core facility capacity raised by 1,750 tons per annum to about 17,750 tons; about 12,000 tons utilised in FY26, with full utilisation expected by year-end in single shift at Unit 1.

Wembley capacity consolidated from four old distributor units into one new integrated facility with about 3x earlier capacity; management expects a turnover of INR250-300 crore from this setup using nitrocellulose and polyurethane products.
Wembley manufacturing facility is fully operational, consolidating multiple production lines.
Formula transfers for acrylic and polyester systems are complete; commercial trials underway with production expected in Q1 FY27. UV technology transfer is on track for Q1.
FY27 capex of about INR5-6 crore planned for acrylic production; most FY26 capex went to consolidating Wembley and Welcome sites.

Polyurethane is replacing melamine; melamine is about INR230-240 per litre vs PU about INR450-460 per litre, with PU about 10% higher per square foot on coverage.

Premium segment competition from large players is seen as limited because specification is driven by architects and designers; mass segment competition is more intense and is addressed through retailer margins and exclusivity.
About 80% of revenue comes from North India (Delhi NCR, Punjab, Haryana, UP, UK, Rajasthan, MP) and about 20% from West and South; 5 of 20 depots opened last year in South and West.
Management said the Indian furniture industry is shifting to local manufacturing after BIS implementation, which supports OEM and institutional demand.

543687|2026-03.headline: FY26 revenue rose 20% to Rs 1,138 crore and EBITDA 34% to Rs 101 crore, while branded formulation grew only 3%.

Growth was driven by domestic institutional formulation (+15%), exports recovery and a 37% rise in domestic active ingredient sales, while branded formulation was muted at 3% due to uneven monsoon and channel destocking. The technical plant reached PBT break-even in FY26, and management guided FY27 revenue growth of 18-20%.

segments.commentary: FY26 growth of 15%, described as consistent across the year.

segments.name: Domestic active ingredient (technical)

qa_highlights.answer: Management said technical EBITDA is about 5% at 65-70% utilisation, improving about 75 bps a year, reaching up to 10% in four to five years. Analyst notes differ on the 8-10% optimum level, which management says takes two to three years.

qa_highlights.question: How does the herbicide shift affect margins and capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the herbicide move is a relocation to a separate site with capacity improvement, and the Rs 50 crore capex covers units 2 and 3 this year; margin improvement is expected to reach double digits in two years.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of El Nino and monsoon on H1 FY27 demand?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no impact so far in Q1 and that even distribution of rain is key; a 2-4% rainfall shortfall would not hurt the season, but an extended dry spell could.

qa_highlights.question: Export growth drivers and margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said exports have GP of 15-20% and EBITDA of 10-12%, with new country registrations continuing and a new team created; Gulf shipments are affected but not stopped.

qa_highlights.question: Why did branded formulation grow only 3%?

543687|2026-09.headline: Dharmaj Crop Guard cut FY27 growth guidance to single-digit from 18-20%, as Q2 revenue fell 4% to Rs 332.6 crore on a weak monsoon and technical slump.
543687|2026-09.overview: H1 FY27 revenue held flat at Rs 716.7 crore and PAT rose 3% to Rs 51.3 crore, but Q2 revenue fell 4% YoY and EBITDA margin compressed to 7.3% from 9.2%. Management attributed the weakness to an 87% of LPA monsoon, a technical business down 27% in Q2 on West Asia-linked input cost and demand disruption, and higher raw material costs flowing through COGS. FY27 revenue guidance was reduced to single-digit growth from the earlier 18-20%. Management reiterated the Rs 2,000 crore revenue target for 2030 and said the herbicide facility remains on track.

segments.commentary: Grew 2% YoY in Q2 and 3% in H1; contributed 55% of H1 FY27 revenue.

segments.name: Branded (blended) formulation
segments.commentary: Grew 5% YoY in Q2 and 2% in H1 as weak Kharif farmer consumption held back growth; contributed 19% of H1 revenue.

segments.name: Export
segments.commentary: Flat YoY in Q2; H1 export grew 50% YoY to Rs 60 crore, now 8% of revenue vs 6% last year.

segments.name: Technical
segments.commentary: Revenue down 27% YoY in Q2 and 20% in H1 on West Asia-linked input pricing and demand disruption; 18% of H1 revenue vs 22% a year earlier. Production aligned to captive formulation needs.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth now expected to be single-digit, down from the earlier 18-20% guidance that assumed a normal monsoon.
Management expects to restore technical margins through cost pass-through to customers over Q3 FY27.
H2 focus: push higher exports, sustain domestic formulation, and restore technical margins.
Dharmaj 2030 target of Rs 2,000 crore revenue reconfirmed; management says it is on track, with about three years left.
Herbicide facility near Ahmedabad (Kerala GIDC) remains on track for commissioning, with production cycle ahead of next Kharif season.
capex_capacity: Capital work-in-progress Rs 11.7 crore at 30 Sep 2026 vs Rs 6.2 crore at March 2026, reflecting spend on the herbicide facility.
New herbicide facility to release capacity at the existing site; herbicide production cycle begins ahead of next Kharif.
Technical capacity aligned to captive formulation requirement to keep plant utilised; three new technical products added, with 2-3 products now backward-integrated.
demand_pricing: Monsoon rainfall at 87% of LPA per IMD, fourth lowest since 2001 and weakest since 2015; weakness concentrated in Western India.
Technical market hit by West Asia crisis affecting input prices and demand; merchant market realisation described as steady.

Operating expenses down 14% YoY to Rs 37.6 crore in Q2, partly offsetting gross margin compression.
Management says there is no sales return policy and no significant channel inventory issue.

qa_highlights.question: How is the company positioned for FY28 and how will formulation growth return?
qa_highlights.answer: Vikas Agarwal said the weak season is rainfall-driven and the company remains on track for Rs 2,000 crore by 2030. Ramesh Talavia said the rainfall shortfall was mainly in Western India, with East and North not affected, and that the company will focus on recovering there.

qa_highlights.question: Will there be channel returns or inventory pressure given the sector downturn?
qa_highlights.answer: Talavia said company policy is no sales returns and it controls this by working to need-based orders. He said there is no major inventory issue and that the company expects single-digit growth by year-end.

qa_highlights.question: What technical molecules and geographies are targeted to support the Rs 2,000 crore vision?
qa_highlights.answer: Talavia said R&D and pilot work has added three new technical products, with 2-3 already backward-integrated. Priority is captive consumption for B2C and B2B formulations, with small technical sales. Export registrations have started coming in.

risks_watch: Single-digit FY27 growth implies a steep H2 ramp versus H1 flat revenue; monitor Q3 delivery.
Technical margin recovery depends on pricing pass-through, which management targets over Q3 FY27; watch gross margin trajectory from 18.6%.

Herbicide facility commissioning timeline and its ramp-up before next Kharif.
Working capital: inventory fell to Rs 174 crore and receivables to Rs 409.9 crore; monitor for collection stress in a weak season.
Export momentum must be sustained to offset weak technical and branded volumes.

543689|2026-03.headline: Uniparts Q4 FY26 revenue rose 34% YoY to INR339 crores with EBITDA margin of 24%; management guides FY27 growth in line with FY26's 21%.

FY26 revenue grew 21%, above the mid-teens guidance given earlier. Management said the agriculture and construction cycle is turning, with new business wins of over INR225 crores annualised in the trailing 12 months. A fire at the Ludhiana finishing shop in Q3 was handled via interim arrangements and is covered by insurance, with normal operations expected by year-end. Management said the company remains net debt free with INR160 crores net cash.

qa_highlights.question: Will the fire affect margins, and when will the plant be back?

qa_highlights.question: Is the 3PL revenue share down because of tractor weakness, and has market share been lost?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the company grew with construction customers as a derisking step; 3PL and PMP are now about 50-50, and no market share has been lost.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 85% working capital improvement sustainable (155 to 136 days)?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory days fell from 146 in FY25 to 134 in FY26; receivable and payable days are now close to par. Management expects these levels to be sustainable, though absolute inventory is rising with OEM backlog orders.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the acquisition and how should capital allocation be viewed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about a dozen targets were evaluated since IPO, with two near-deals that fell through. Any target must add a third platform, be manageable in size, and be ROE/ROCE accretive. The Q3 special dividend followed a deal that was not pursued.

qa_highlights.question: What is the total order book and how has win conversion changed?

543732|2026-03.headline: Radiant CMS standalone revenue flat in FY26 at INR1.69 trillion cash handled; consolidated PAT fell to INR280 million from INR470 million on fintech losses.

Consolidated PAT dropped to INR280 million from INR470 million, mainly from losses at fintech subsidiary Radiant Acemoney after the PIDF subsidy ended in December 2025. 543732|2026-06.headline: Radiant Q1 FY27 standalone EBITDA margin fell to 13.5% from 15.9% on manpower costs, with standalone revenue up 7% on the IDBI mandate.

Standalone EBITDA margin fell to 13.5% from 15.9% a year ago because of gunmen costs, minimum wage hikes and southern-state licensed gunmen shortages. Consolidated PAT was Rs 52 million versus Rs 57 million, as Radiant Acemoney losses narrowed. Management is pinning margin recovery on price revisions it expects to complete in Q2, plus revenue growth and cost control.

segments.name: Standalone cash management
segments.commentary: Revenue up 7% with IDBI mandate; BFSI and organised retail grew well, while railways, petroleum and e-commerce were sluggish. Management says the e-commerce logistics decline has been arrested and turned positive.

segments.name: Radiant Valuable Logistics (RVL)
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 22.1 million in Q1 FY27, up 24% QoQ; management expects breakeven in the current quarter. Customers have been conservative in movements amid volatility linked to the war.

segments.name: Radiant Acemoney (fintech subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Losses narrowed QoQ after PIDF subsidy ended in December 2025 and fixed costs were cut. Network of over 20,000 BCs, 58,000+ Soundboxes deployed cumulatively, Rs 170 crore transaction volume in Q1; management targets breakeven in September and a full quarter breakeven in Q3.

FY27 standalone EBITDA margin guided at 17%-18%, after factoring in price increases (per Q&A).

Acemoney: plans to deploy 50,000 Soundboxes in FY27, with 60%-70% already in order book; transaction revenues more meaningful in FY28.
Payment aggregator licence: revised application to be resubmitted by end-August or early September; licence expected by January or February 2027; business launch planned in FY28.
capex_capacity: Network of roughly 1,50,000 POS machines and 20,000 business correspondents cited as distribution base; spread across about 15,000 pin codes.
Acemoney plans 50,000 Soundbox deployments in FY27; cumulative 58,000+ deployed.

Management said manpower is now deployed only for Soundbox/QR deployment and UPI white-label/fintech software work, with a technology team handling the rest.
demand_pricing: Standalone margin pressure from employee costs, driver and gunman costs, and cash executive service charges; minimum wage hikes in northern states and Karnataka; licensed gunmen shortage in southern states.
Long-tail smaller points are moving to payments banks and some banks have stopped the service; points from banks are not growing, which is limiting volume growth.
Last card-rate price revision was in 2021 per management; price revision is being negotiated through the Cash Logistics Association and IBA.

Management claims pricing is 10-20 bps for merchants versus 150-200 bps for credit card transactions.

qa_highlights.question: What is the big picture for Acemoney and its breakeven?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the acquisition aimed at leveraging the 20,000-BC network and recovering around Rs 30 crore of annual revenue lost to payments banks. Breakeven is targeted for September, with a full quarter in Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Payment aggregator licence status?
qa_highlights.answer: Revised application is yet to be filed, to be resubmitted by end-September or early September; licence expected by January-February 2027 and business to start in FY28.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said it would give the idea serious thought and bring it to the board at the coming meeting.

EBITDA was Rs 41.6 crore (29.4% margin) and PAT was Rs 25.2 crore (17.8% margin). Management framed the quarter as the start of a broader growth phase, citing the Indonesia programme, exports, components, and a planned US greenfield plant (Project Mayflower). EV transmission deliveries were soft in Q1 and management expects a pickup in schedules over the next three quarters.

segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 5.7 crore; described as subdued in Q1 as a Tata localisation programme slowed. Management says quarterly run-rate expectation rises from Rs 6.5-7 crore to Rs 10-12 crore.

segments.name: Components
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 34.4 crore, +83% YoY, helped by improved realisations, higher precision-component mix and export growth.

segments.name: Other (NexTrac, ALH, Synchro, aftermarket, other income)
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 21.4 crore vs Rs 6.5 crore in Q1 FY26.

543814|2026-03.headline: FY26 total income rose 85% to Rs 57.62 crore and PAT to Rs 2.44 crore, but H2 margins fell on rupee-driven input costs, depreciation and marketing spend.
543814|2026-03.overview: Management reported FY26 total income of Rs 57.62 crore (up 85% YoY), EBITDA of Rs 6.31 crore (up 48.34%) and PAT of Rs 2.44 crore (up 14.76%). Capacity utilisation at the Changodar plant rose to roughly 2,500-3,000 MTPA from about 1,200 MTPA previously, against 4,800 MTPA installed. H2 PAT and margins were lower than H1, which management attributed to rupee depreciation (about 84-85 to 93-94 per USD) flowing through average-cost inventory, about Rs 1.5 crore of extra depreciation, higher working-capital interest, and D2C marketing and SKU expansion (24 SKUs versus 3 last year). Management also said H2 sales were weaker because most of the festive selling was completed before Diwali.

financial_highlights.change: from around Rs 5 crore last year

segments.name: B2B cashew processing
segments.commentary: Core business; capacity utilisation of 2,500-3,000 MTPA in FY26 against 4,800 MTPA installed. Management says FY26 volume growth was the sole driver of revenue growth, with no price or mix contribution.

segments.name: B2C / D2C (DriFrutz brand)
segments.commentary: Revenue to date is very small, around Rs 50-60 lakh including gifting. Target is 10% of total revenue, with timing unclear (six months to a couple of years). Listed on Amazon, Flipkart, DriFrutz website and Hyperpure; Blinkit in discussion.

segments.name: By-products (shell, husk)
segments.commentary: About 70% of raw cashew comes out as shell, sold directly to CNSL processors, and about 2-2.5% as husk, also sold. No CNSL or pellet processing is done in-house.

EBITDA margin target of 12-15%; implied PAT margin of roughly 5-7% per management.
B2C target of 10% of revenue in FY27, with timing uncertain.
Management targets a 40-45% revenue CAGR over the next three years.
Debt-to-equity to peak at about 0.6 by year-end and stay below 1:1; management aims to fund further growth through debt rather than equity for now.
Management expects about one more month to pass through the rupee-driven cost increases before pricing is fully absorbed; a 15-20 day Diwali production break is expected in H2.
capex_capacity: Changodar plant installed capacity 4,800 MTPA; utilisation about 2,500-3,000 MTPA in FY26.
Automation at about 80% across the seven processing stages (deshelling, boiling, moisture control, peeling, colour sorting).
Management aims for 300-400 tonnes per month of deshelling output in the first six months of FY27 and said about 1,800 tonnes of capacity is still unused.
Working-capital bank facility raised last year; the company plans to reach full utilisation by year-end without further debt raising.
demand_pricing: Raw cashew cost rose from about Rs 110-120/kg a couple of years ago to Rs 140-150 last year and about Rs 170-175 now.
Rupee moved from about 84-85 to 93-94 per USD by March 2026. Average-cost inventory accounting carried this into COGS in H2.
Fuel price rises are raising transport costs; the company is still absorbing the cost increases.
Sourcing shifted from West Africa to Tanzania and Ghana in Dec-Feb; local Indian crop is priced higher.
Management says the market is softer from February, and a large part of the festive sales is done about 10 days before Diwali.
Management says big established brands are not yet direct competitors; it cited quick commerce growth and positive packaging feedback from Blinkit.
Hyperpure takes a 15-20% margin; Blinkit listing is still in discussion.

qa_highlights.question: Why did H2 margins and PAT fall versus H1, and why was H2 revenue weaker?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a roughly Rs 1.5 crore depreciation hit, rupee depreciation from 84-85 to 93-94 flowing through average-cost inventory, higher interest on newly drawn working capital, and D2C marketing and SKU expansion. Most festive sales were done before Diwali, and the market weakened from February.

qa_highlights.question: What EBITDA and PAT margins should be expected going forward, and what is the war impact on imported raw material?
qa_highlights.answer: EBITDA target is 12-15%, with PAT around 5-7%. The rupee move and higher fuel costs are being absorbed gradually; management expects about one month more before pricing catches up fully, and flagged that retail spending will weigh on profit.

qa_highlights.question: What is the B2B and B2C revenue split and the FY27 outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: B2C plus gifting is very small, around Rs 50-60 lakh to date. The first target is 10% of revenue, and the timeline ranges from six months to a couple of years.

qa_highlights.question: What is the inventory build-up and debt position?
qa_highlights.answer: About 25-30% of stock is cashew with testa residue that needs manual cleaning. This is sent to home-based labour, which has grown from about 30 to around 80 workers. Borrowings rose from about Rs 5 crore to over Rs 10 crore on working-capital needs from higher raw-material prices and capacity. Peak D/E is expected at about 0.6, below 1:1.

qa_highlights.question: What is the sourcing mix and the by-product outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 raw cashew was sourced mainly from West and East Africa, then Tanzania and Ghana. Shell is about 70% of raw cashew input and husk about 2-2.5%, both sold rather than processed; these ratios are expected to hold at higher volumes.

qa_highlights.question: What are the channel economics, CAC and competitive positioning in D2C?
qa_highlights.answer: No CAC has been calculated yet; Hyperpure and Amazon marketing is funded from the marketing budget. Management does not see established brands as direct competitors yet and is focused on positioning DriFrutz in the premium segment.

risks_watch: Gross and EBITDA margins are under pressure from rupee depreciation, average-cost inventory accounting, and fuel-driven transport costs. Watch whether the 12-15% EBITDA target holds in H1 FY27.
Inventory of around Rs 18 crore, including roughly 25-30% of stock that needs manual deshelling, is a working-capital and dead-stock risk.
Borrowings have roughly doubled to over Rs 10 crore and finance cost rose to Rs 1.3 crore from Rs 0.48 crore; peak D/E target is about 0.6.
B2C scale-up depends on quick commerce and gifting, which are still at very small revenue levels. The 10% target has no firm timeline.
Raw cashew prices are rising every year, and sourcing depends mainly on African origins.
